definition_zh: 不；没有；并非；不太
definition_en: used to negate a verb, adjective or whole clause; also used to deny a noun phrase or to soften what is said
core_image: 一扇紧闭的门上挂着一块木牌，牌上只写着一个表示拒绝的字
scene: 门上挂着一块手写的木牌，路过的人凑近看了又看，随后转身离开。The sign on the door said the shop would not open until noon.
sceneCN: 这里是「不」（第 1 个义项：否定动词、形容词或整个句子），句意为门上的告示说这家店要到中午才开门。图中可辨识物件：木牌、门把手、台阶。

derivatives.zh: 由 can 与 not 合成，义为「不能」，写作一个词
与 not 同出古英语的否定词，义为「零；无」
由 not 与 withstand 加 -ing 构成，义为「尽管；虽然」

senses.title: Used to negate a verb, adjective or clause
senses.titleCN: 不；没有（否定动词、形容词或句子）
senses.definition: used before a verb, adjective or adverb to say that something is not true, does not happen or is not the case
senses.definitionCN: 用在动词、形容词或副词前，表示某事不真实、不发生或不成立
senses.example: The sign on the door said the shop would not open until noon.
senses.exampleCN: 门上的告示说这家店要到中午才开门。
senses.why: The word began as a pronoun meaning no thing, and in unstressed positions it shrank into a bare negator that could sit in front of any verb and turn it negative.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是一个代词，意思是「没有东西」；在非重读的位置上它缩成一个光秃秃的否定词，可以放在任何动词前把动词变成否定。

senses.title: Used to deny a noun phrase or a statement
senses.titleCN: 不是；并非（否定名词或整句话）
senses.definition: used before a noun phrase, or in a short answer, to reject it rather than to describe an action
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词短语前，或用于简短回答，表示否定对方所说的内容，而不是描述某个动作
senses.example: Not everyone in the room agreed with the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里并非每个人都同意这个计划。
senses.why: Once the pronoun lost its noun, the negator could stand before any phrase, not only before a verb, so it learned to reject a subject or an entire statement.
senses.whyCN: 代词丢掉后面的名词之后，这个否定词可以站在任何短语前面，而不只是动词前面，于是它学会了否定一个主语或整句话。

senses.title: Used to soften or limit what is said
senses.titleCN: 不太；并不（用于委婉或减弱语气）
senses.definition: used before a word to weaken a claim, as in not very, not quite or not necessarily
senses.definitionCN: 用在某个词前减弱语气，如 not very、not quite 或 not necessarily
senses.example: The result was not unexpected, but it was still a shock.
senses.exampleCN: 这个结果并不意外，但还是让人吃惊。
senses.why: A flat denial is blunt, so English puts the same negator in front of a weaker word to hold back the claim; the sentence stays negative while the tone turns careful.
senses.whyCN: 直截了当的否定太冲，于是英语把同一个否定词放在更弱的词前面，用来收住话头；句子仍是否定，语气却变得谨慎。

intro.en: Not began as a pronoun for no thing and was shortened into the general English negator; its oldest surviving relative is the word for nought.
intro.cn: not 最初是一个表示「没有东西」的代词，后来缩短成英语里通用的否定词；它现存最老的亲族是表示「零」的那个词。

items.en: Nā meant never or not and wiht meant a thing, so nāwiht said no thing and could stand alone as a pronoun.
items.cn: nā 表示「从不、不」，wiht 表示「东西」，因此 nāwiht 说的是「没有东西」，可以单独作代词使用。

items.en: In quick speech the pronoun was contracted to nāht, which served as the word for nothing and later for zero.
items.cn: 在快速的口语里，这个代词缩成 nāht，既用来表示「没有什么」，后来也用来表示「零」。

items.en: The unstressed form not split off from nought and took over as the ordinary negator, replacing the older pattern of ne before the verb.
items.cn: 非重读形式 not 从 nought 里分出来，取代了旧的「ne 加动词」格式，成为日常的否定词。

items.en: Do-support spread, and not attached itself to do, does and did, which is why modern questions and emphatic statements still use do not.
items.cn: 助动词 do 的用法扩展开来，not 便附着在 do、does、did 上，所以现代的问句和强调句仍用 do not。

items.en: Modern English also contracts not to n't, and keeps it in fixed frames such as not only and if not, where the negation shapes the whole sentence.
items.cn: 现代英语还把 not 缩写成 n't，并把它保留在 not only、if not 这类固定框架里，那里的否定塑造着整个句子。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that share the old no-thing stem; the near-meaning group collects the other ways English denies or zeroes out a statement.
note.cn: 形近组收共享古老「无物」词干的词；近义组收英语中其他表示否定或归零的说法。

entries.definition: An older spelling of nought, meaning nothing or zero.
entries.definitionCN: nought 的较旧拼写，意为「无」或「零」。

entries.definition: The number zero, and in older use nothing at all.
entries.definitionCN: 数字零，旧时也指「什么都没有」。

entries.definition: A preposition meaning in spite of, built with not at its head.
entries.definitionCN: 以 not 开头的介词，义为「尽管」。

entries.definition: A determiner that denies the existence of a thing, as in no money.
entries.definitionCN: 限定词，否认某物的存在，如 no money。

entries.definition: At no time, the negator used for time rather than for a single action.
entries.definitionCN: 在任何时候都不，是用来否定时间的否定词。

entries.definition: Not one, or not any, a pronoun that stands in for a negated quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 一个也不、任何也不，是代替被否定数量的代词。

normalIntro.en: The word is a shrunken pronoun for no thing, and its whole history is a drift from a standalone word toward a small negator that hooks onto verbs.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个缩小的「无物」代词，它的全部历史就是从独立词漂移成一个钩在动词前的小否定词。

normal.en: Old English nāwiht was nā plus wiht, no plus thing, so not and nothing come from the same source.
normal.cn: 古英语 nāwiht 是 nā 加 wiht，即「不」加「东西」，所以 not 与 nothing 同出一源。

normal.en: The unstressed form not broke away from nought and became the everyday way to deny a verb.
normal.cn: 非重读形式 not 从 nought 里脱离出来，成为日常否定动词的方式。

normal.en: Modern questions use do-support, so the negator rides on do, does or did rather than sitting alone.
normal.cn: 现代问句用助动词 do 支撑，所以否定词搭在 do、does 或 did 上，而不是单独站着。

normal.en: The contraction n't keeps the same word in a shorter shape, as in isn't and don't.
normal.cn: 缩写 n't 是同一个词的短形，如 isn't 与 don't。

normal.en: Fixed frames such as not only and if not show that not can negate a whole structure, not just one word.
normal.cn: not only 与 if not 这类固定框架说明，not 能否定整个结构，而不只是一个词。

abstract.en: A word that once meant no thing ended up as the smallest hinge in English grammar, turning any sentence the other way.
abstract.cn: 一个曾经表示「没有东西」的词，最后成了英语语法里最小的铰链，把任何句子转向反面。

abstract.en: Negation always costs a word, and English chose to shorten its oldest denial until only three letters were left.
abstract.cn: 否定总要花掉一个词，英语选择把最古老的否认一再缩短，直到只剩下三个字母。

abstract.en: Not is the quiet tool that lets a language say what is absent without naming it.
abstract.cn: not 是语言里一件安静的工具，让人不必说出缺席之物，也能说出它的缺席。

examples.en: The sign on the door said the shop would not open until noon.
examples.cn: 门上的告示说这家店要到中午才开门。

examples.en: Not everyone in the room agreed with the plan.
examples.cn: 房间里并非每个人都同意这个计划。

examples.en: The result was not unexpected, but it was still a shock.
examples.cn: 这个结果并不意外，但还是让人吃惊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诺特」——门上挂着牌子，只写一个否定的字；not 就是不。

root: 古英语 nāwiht（nā「不」加 wiht「东西」，即「无物」）缩为 nāht，中古英语非重读形式 not 独立出来，取代 ne 加动词的旧否定格式；同源词有 nought、nothing。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the denial of a thing; it then spreads to verbs and clauses, to short answers, and to softened or limited claims.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是对「有某物」的否认；义项由此扩展到动词与句子、简短回答，以及被减弱或限制的说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wooden sign hanging on a shut door, carrying a single mark of refusal.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇紧闭的门上挂着一块木牌，牌上只有一个表示拒绝的记号。

branches.en: a door sign that turns a visitor away
branches.cn: 把来客挡回去的门上告示

branches.en: a switch flipped to the off position
branches.cn: 被扳到关闭位置的开关

branches.en: a raised hand rejecting a whole proposal
branches.cn: 举手否决整个提案

branches.en: a careful speaker holding back a strong word
branches.cn: 措辞谨慎的人收住一个重词

branches.en: one small word denying an act and denying a claim
branches.cn: 同一个短词既否定动作，也否定说法

intro.en: The word is built from an Old English negative particle and a noun for thing, then shortened and joined to English auxiliaries and contractions.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语的否定小词与表示「东西」的名词构成，之后被缩短，并与英语助动词和缩写形式结合。

latinIntro.en: Not has no reliable Latin cognate; Latin negates with non and nihil, words of a different formation, so no Latin entry is listed.
latinIntro.cn: not 没有可靠的拉丁同族词；拉丁语用「non」与「nihil」表示否定，构词方式不同，因此不列拉丁词条。

definition_zh: 尤其；显著地；值得注意的是
definition_en: especially, or in a way that is easy to notice
core_image: 一群人中只有一个人穿亮色外套，视线自然落在他身上
scene: 报告在列举增长地区时，特别点出了一个省。Several provinces grew, notably the coastal one.
sceneCN: 这里指从一组中特别举出一项（第 3 个义项：举出突出例子）；句意为几个省都有增长，尤其是沿海那个省；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 尤其；显著地；值得注意的是

senses.title: Especially
senses.definition: more than others, in a way that deserves attention
senses.definitionCN: 比其余更突出，值得注意
senses.example: The region is notably dry in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区夏季格外干燥。
senses.why: The adverb raises one item above its neighbours without saying it is the only one.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词把某一项抬到邻项之上，却不说它是唯一的一项。

senses.title: Sentence-opening highlight
senses.definition: at the start of a sentence, drawing attention to the fact that follows
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首，把注意力引向随后的事实
senses.example: Notably, no one objected to the change.
senses.exampleCN: 值得注意的是，没有人反对这一改动。
senses.why: The initial position tells the reader that the next clause is the point worth remembering.
senses.whyCN: 句首位置告诉读者，下一个小句才是值得记住的要点。

senses.title: Introducing a striking example
senses.definition: used before a noun phrase to single out an example
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词短语前，单举一个例子
senses.example: Some countries, notably Germany, changed their policy.
senses.exampleCN: 一些国家，尤其是德国，改变了政策。
senses.why: The word introduces a specimen that makes the general claim concrete.
senses.whyCN: 这个词引出一个样本，使一般性说法变得具体。

senses.title: To a noticeable degree
senses.definition: used before an adjective to say a quality is easy to observe
senses.definitionCN: 放在形容词前，表示某种性质容易观察到
senses.example: The two versions are notably different in tone.
senses.exampleCN: 两个版本在语气上明显不同。
senses.why: Here it modifies an adjective and measures visibility, close to noticeably.
senses.whyCN: 这里修饰形容词，衡量的是「可见程度」，接近「明显地」。

senses.title: Notably absent
senses.definition: in the fixed pattern notably absent, conspicuous by not being there
senses.definitionCN: 在固定搭配「显著缺席」中，指因不在场而引人注意
senses.example: Notably absent from the report was any mention of cost.
senses.exampleCN: 报告中明显缺席的是任何关于成本的提及。
senses.why: The phrase turns absence itself into the noticeable fact, a common rhetorical move.
senses.whyCN: 这一短语把「缺席」本身变成引人注意的事实，是常见的修辞手法。

senses.title: Before a comparative
senses.definition: used with a comparative to mark a difference larger than expected
senses.definitionCN: 与比较级连用，标记超出预期的差距
senses.example: This year's harvest was notably better than last year's.
senses.exampleCN: 今年的收成明显好于去年。
senses.why: With comparatives the word enlarges the gap rather than merely reporting it.
senses.whyCN: 与比较级连用时，它放大差距，而不只是报告差距。

senses.title: Academic evidence marker
senses.titleCN: 学术写作中的证据标记
senses.definition: in research writing, flagging the observation that carries the argument
senses.definitionCN: 在研究写作中，标出支撑论证的那项观察
senses.example: The study found, notably, that older users adapted faster.
senses.exampleCN: 研究发现，值得注意的是，年长用户适应得更快。
senses.why: The marker tells readers which result the author treats as decisive.
senses.whyCN: 这个标记告诉读者，作者把哪一项结果当作关键。

senses.title: In a way that attracts notice
senses.definition: of behaviour or appearance, in a manner that draws attention
senses.definitionCN: 指行为或外表以引人注意的方式
senses.example: The house was notably decorated for the festival.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋房子为节日做了惹眼的装饰。
senses.why: The older manner sense describes doing something in a way that is meant to be seen.
senses.whyCN: 较早的方式义描述以「就是要被看见」的方式做事。

intro.en: Notably comes from the Latin adjective for worthy of note, through French, plus the English adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词来自拉丁语「值得注意的」形容词，经法语，再加英语副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The noun nota means a mark, sign or written note.
items.cn: 名词意为「记号、标记、注记」。

items.en: The verb notare means to mark or observe, and gives the stem of the adjective.
items.cn: 动词意为「标记、注意」，提供形容词词干。

items.en: The adjective notabilis means worthy of note or remarkable.
items.cn: 形容词意为「值得注意的、显著的」。

items.en: Old French notable and English notable carry the adjective into use.
items.cn: 古法语与英语形容词把它带入使用。

items.en: The adverb adds the usual suffix; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 副词加常见后缀；英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: Modern prose uses notably both to single out examples and to measure visible degree.
items.cn: 现代散文既用它单举例子，也用它衡量可见的程度。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin mark-root; the second group contrasts highlighting an example with intensifying a degree.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「记号」词根；第二组对照「举出例子」与「加强程度」。

entries.definition: Worthy of attention; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 值得注意的；副词的形容词基形。

entries.definition: The state of being important enough to be noticed.
entries.definitionCN: 重要到足以被注意的状态。

entries.definition: A system of written marks or symbols.
entries.definitionCN: 书写的记号或符号系统。

entries.definition: To mark something with symbols or notes.
entries.definitionCN: 用符号或注记标出某物。

entries.definition: Above all, or to a high degree; broader than notably because it also intensifies.
entries.definitionCN: 首先、格外；比「值得注意的是」更宽，因为它也能单纯加强程度。

entries.definition: Specifically or especially; often narrower and more precise than especially.
entries.definitionCN: 具体地或尤其；常比「尤其」更窄、更精确。

entries.definition: In a surprising or striking degree.
entries.definitionCN: 以达到令人惊讶或醒目的程度。

entries.definition: In a way that is clearly visible or attracting attention.
entries.definitionCN: 以清楚可见或引人注意的方式。

entries.definition: A phrase singling out one member of a group.
entries.definitionCN: 从一组中单举一个成员的说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real mark-root and the real split between singling out an example and measuring degree.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「记号」词根，并区分「单举例子」与「衡量程度」。

normal.en: The root is a mark, so notably points to the item with a mark beside it.
normal.cn: 词根是「记号」，所以这个词指向旁边打了记号的那一项。

normal.en: Notably absent is a sentence about what is not there, which makes the gap loud.
normal.cn: 「显著缺席」说的是不在场的东西，反而让空缺更响。

normal.en: Before a comparative it says the gap is bigger than you might assume.
normal.cn: 放在比较级前，它说明差距比你以为的更大。

normal.en: In academic prose it quietly tells the reader which result matters.
normal.cn: 在学术文字里，它悄悄告诉读者哪项结果才重要。

normal.en: Most notably often opens a list that ends with the strongest case.
normal.cn: 「最值得注意的是」常引出一个以最强例子收尾的清单。

abstract.en: A mark on a page is a promise that this part will be looked at twice.
abstract.cn: 纸上的记号是一种承诺：这一处会被再看一眼。

abstract.en: Attention is a scarce resource, and the word spends it on one item.
abstract.cn: 注意力是稀缺资源，这个词把它花在其中一项上。

abstract.en: Saying what is notably absent is a way of describing a room by its missing chair.
abstract.cn: 说某物显著缺席，就是靠少了一把椅子来描述一间屋子。

examples.en: The team improved, notably in defence.
examples.cn: 球队进步了，尤其是在防守方面。

examples.en: Notably, the two accounts disagree on the date.
examples.cn: 值得注意的是，两份记载在日期上并不一致。

examples.en: The second method is notably cheaper to run.
examples.cn: 第二种方法运行起来明显更便宜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「诺特布利」——被特别记在备忘录上，所以显著

root: 拉丁语名词「记号」派生动词「标记、注意」，再构成形容词「值得注意的」；英语经法语借入形容词后加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate emphasis above neighbours, sentence-opening highlight, a singled-out example, visible degree, conspicuous absence, enlarged comparison, academic evidence marking and attention-drawing manner.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理高于邻项的强调、句首提示、单举例子、可见程度、显著缺席、放大的比较、学术证据标记，以及引人注意的方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one bright coat in a crowd, pulling every glance toward it.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群里一件亮色外套，把视线都拉过去。

branches.en: THE RAISED ITEM: one thing stands above its neighbours.
branches.cn: 被抬高的一项：某物高于邻项。

branches.en: THE FLAG: the sentence-opening highlight and the academic evidence marker.
branches.cn: 旗标：句首提示与学术证据标记。

branches.en: THE EXAMPLE: a specimen that makes the general claim concrete.
branches.cn: 例子：使一般说法具体化的样本。

branches.en: THE MEASURED DEGREE: visible quality and an enlarged comparison.
branches.cn: 可测的程度：可见的性质与被放大的比较。

branches.en: THE NOTICED ABSENCE AND MANNER: the gap heard loud, and behaviour meant to be seen.
branches.cn: 被注意的空缺与方式：响亮的缺席，以及有意被看见的举止。

intro.en: Notably is a Latin mark-noun, a Latin verb stem, an adjective suffix, a French layer and an English adverb suffix.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「记号」名词、「标记」动词词干、形容词后缀、法语层与英语副词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The noun for a mark builds a verb of marking and an adjective of being worth a mark, from which English takes the adverb.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「记号」的名词构成「标记」动词与「值得被标记」的形容词，英语由它取得副词。

items.example: The noun is the concrete mark that starts the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是词族起点的具体记号。

items.example: The verb turns the mark into an act of noticing.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把记号变成「注意到」的动作。

items.example: The suffix builds an adjective of worthiness.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表「值得」的形容词。

items.example: The adjective says a thing deserves a mark beside it.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词说某物值得在旁边打个记号。

items.example: English keeps the adjective for people and events worth attention.
items.exampleCN: 英语保留这个形容词，用于值得注意的人与事。

items.example: The noun names the social result of being noticed.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名被注意带来的社会结果。

items.example: A different branch of the family names written symbols.
items.exampleCN: 词族的另一支命名书写的符号。

items.example: The verb returns to the physical act of marking.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词回到「做记号」的具体动作。

items.example: The suffix turns notable into a highlighting adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成提示性副词。

definition_zh: 笔记；便条；音符；注意；记下
definition_en: a short written record or message; a single musical sound; attention; and the act of noticing or writing something down
core_image: 纸页边缘写满小字，一张折好的短笺压在书页之间
scene: 厨房的桌上压着一张折好的纸条，字迹很急，末尾没有署名。She read the note twice before answering.
sceneCN: 这里是「便条、短笺」（第 2 个义项：写在纸上的简短留言），句意为她把那张便条读了两遍才回话。图中可辨识物件：折好的纸条、厨房桌、笔。

derivatives.zh: 由 note 与 book 复合而成，义为「笔记本」
由 note 的拉丁词干加 -able 构成，义为「值得注意的；显著的」
由拉丁词干 notare 加 -tion 构成，义为「记号系统；记谱法」

senses.title: A short written record of something heard or read
senses.definition: a short written record, especially of what a speaker said or what a reader wants to remember
senses.definitionCN: 简短的书面记录，尤指记下讲者所说或读者想记住的内容
senses.example: She filled three pages with notes during the lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 讲座期间她记满了三页笔记。
senses.why: Latin nota was a mark or written sign, and the first English sense kept that idea of a small written trace left behind for later use.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 nota 是「记号、写下的符号」，英语最初的意思保留了这种「为以后使用而留下的小小书写痕迹」。

senses.title: A short written message
senses.definition: a short informal letter or message written on a piece of paper
senses.definitionCN: 写在纸上的简短、非正式的留言或信
senses.example: She read the note twice before answering.
senses.exampleCN: 她把那张便条读了两遍才回话。
senses.why: Because any written mark can be handed to someone else, note slid from a private record to a message left for another person, usually brief and casual.
senses.whyCN: 既然任何书写记号都能交给别人，note 就从私人记录滑向留给别人的留言，通常简短而随意。

senses.title: A single musical sound or its written sign
senses.definition: a single sound in music, or the written symbol that stands for it
senses.definitionCN: 音乐中的单个音，或代表这个音的书写符号
senses.example: She held the last note longer than the others.
senses.exampleCN: 她把最后一个音拖得比别的音更长。
senses.why: A musical tone can be written down like any other sign, so the word for a written mark came to name one printed dot on a staff and then the sound it stands for.
senses.whyCN: 乐音也能像别的符号一样写下来，于是表示书写记号的词先指谱线中的一个点，再指它所代表的那个音。

senses.title: Attention or notice given to something
senses.definition: attention given to something, especially in the phrase take note of
senses.definitionCN: 对某事给予的关注，尤用于 take note of 这一说法
senses.example: Take note of the small changes in the pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 请留意这个图案里细微的变化。
senses.why: A note is something you write so that it will be remembered, and from that comes the sense of giving something enough attention for it to be remembered.
senses.whyCN: 笔记是为了日后记得才写下的东西，由此引申出「给予足够关注、以便记住」的意思。

senses.title: To notice or write something down
senses.definition: to notice something and give it attention, or to write it down so that it is recorded
senses.definitionCN: 注意到某事并加以关注，或把它写下来留作记录
senses.example: He noted the time in the margin of his notebook.
senses.exampleCN: 他把时间记在笔记本的页边。
senses.why: Once the noun means a written trace of attention, the matching verb naturally means the act that produces it, so noting is both watching closely and setting the result on paper.
senses.whyCN: 当名词已经表示「注意力留下的书写痕迹」，与之对应的动词自然就表示产生这个痕迹的动作，所以 noting 既是仔细观察，也是把结果落到纸上。

intro.en: Note comes from a Latin word for a mark or written sign, entered English through Old French, and later grew senses for messages, music and attention.
intro.cn: note 来自拉丁语中表示「记号、书写符号」的词，经古法语进入英语，后来才长出留言、音乐与注意等义项。

items.en: Nota was a mark, a written character or a sign of something, and it is generally connected with the Latin verb for knowing, noscere.
items.cn: nota 是记号、书写符号或某事的标志，一般认为它与拉丁语中表示「认识」的动词 noscere 有关。

items.en: The verb notare meant to mark, to write down or to observe, and it supplied the family of words about noting and notation.
items.cn: 动词 notare 意为标记、写下或观察，由此衍生出与记录和记号系统有关的一族词。

items.en: Old French passed on note as a written mark, a memorandum or a short writing after the Norman period.
items.cn: 诺曼时期之后，古法语把 note 传进英语，意思为书面的记号、备忘或短小的文字。

items.en: Middle English note covered a written record, a melody and a token of something, so the musical sense was already present.
items.cn: 中古英语的 note 已包含书面记录、曲调与某事物的标志，音乐义那时就已经在场。

items.en: Modern English adds the short message, the musical symbol, the sense of attention and the verb, together with the compound banknote for paper money.
items.cn: 现代英语增添了便条、音乐符号、注意等意思和动词用法，还添上表示纸币的复合词 banknote。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin stem nota through English derivatives; the near-meaning group collects the short writings and messages that note resembles.
note.cn: 形近组沿拉丁词干 nota 收英语派生词；近义组收与 note 相近的短小文字与留言。

entries.definition: A system of written symbols, such as the notation used for music.
entries.definitionCN: 书写符号的系统，如音乐所用的记谱法。

entries.definition: Worthy of attention, built from the same stem with -able.
entries.definitionCN: 值得注意的，同一词干加 -able 构成。

entries.definition: A book of blank pages for writing notes.
entries.definitionCN: 用来记笔记、带空白页的本子。

entries.definition: A short written message inside an office or organization.
entries.definitionCN: 办公室或机构内部简短的书面留言。

entries.definition: Information sent from one person to another, in speech, writing or another medium.
entries.definitionCN: 由一人传给另一人的信息，可用口头、书面或其他方式。

entries.definition: A written or stored account of something kept for later reference.
entries.definitionCN: 为日后查阅而保存的书面或存储记载。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin mark that became a small piece of writing, then a message, a musical sign and a act of attention.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词原是拉丁语的「记号」，后来变成一小段文字、一条留言、一个音乐符号，以及一次关注的动作。

normal.en: Latin nota meant a mark or written sign, so every sense of note still involves something set down to be seen again.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 nota 意为记号或书写符号，所以 note 的每个义项都离不开「写下来以便再看」这件事。

normal.en: Notare is the Latin verb to mark or write, and it is the base of notation and notable.
normal.cn: notare 是拉丁语里「标记、书写」的动词，也是 notation 与 notable 的底座。

normal.en: The musical note is simply a written sign on a staff, which is why the same word names the symbol and the sound.
normal.cn: 音乐里的 note 不过是谱线上的一个书写符号，所以同一个词既指符号也指声音。

normal.en: Take note of keeps the physical picture: you write something because you want to keep it in mind.
normal.cn: take note of 保留了那个具体画面：你把它写下来，是因为想把它记在心里。

normal.en: Banknote is a note in the old sense of a written promise to pay, now the paper money itself.
normal.cn: banknote 里的 note 用的是旧义「书面的付款承诺」，今天则直接指那张纸币。

abstract.en: A mark that was meant to be read later became a message meant for someone else, and both still depend on paper holding a thought still.
abstract.cn: 一个本来留给以后自己看的记号，变成了留给别人的留言，两者都依赖纸张把一个念头固定住。

abstract.en: Note shows how writing turns attention into an object: what you noticed becomes something you can hand over.
abstract.cn: note 展示了书写如何把注意力变成物件：你注意到的东西变成可以递交出去的东西。

abstract.en: The same short word can be a page of study, a line of music and a warning, because all three are traces left for a later reader.
abstract.cn: 同一个短词可以是整页的学习、一行音乐，也可以是一句提醒，因为三者都是留给后来读者看的痕迹。

examples.en: She read the note twice before answering.
examples.cn: 她把那张便条读了两遍才回话。

examples.en: She filled three pages with notes during the lecture.
examples.cn: 讲座期间她记满了三页笔记。

examples.en: He noted the time in the margin of his notebook.
examples.cn: 他把时间记在笔记本的页边。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诺特」——桌上压着一张小纸条，几行字就说明了来意；note 就是便条、笔记。

root: 拉丁语 nota（记号、书写符号）与动词 notare（标记、写下），经古法语 note 进入中古英语；同族词有 notable、notation、notebook。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a written mark kept for later; the senses then divide into the record, the message, the musical sign, and attention with its verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「为日后而留下的书写记号」；义项由此分出记录、留言、音乐符号，以及注意和相应的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a page crowded with small handwriting, with a folded slip pressed between the leaves.
core.cn: 核心意象：写满小字的纸页，夹着一张折好的短笺。

branches.en: a page of lecture notes written in a tight hand
branches.cn: 写得密密麻麻的一页讲座笔记

branches.en: a sentence underlined twice in the margin
branches.cn: 页边被划了两道线的句子

branches.en: a folded slip left on a kitchen table
branches.cn: 厨房桌上留下的折好的纸条

branches.en: one held tone at the end of a song
branches.cn: 歌曲结尾一个被拖长的音

branches.en: a reader pausing, then writing a date in the corner
branches.cn: 读者停了一下，在角上写下日期

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin noun for a mark, its verb, and English endings that build its derivatives and compounds.
intro.cn: 这个词立在拉丁语表示「记号」的名词与动词上，再由英语词尾构成它的派生词与复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun nota and its verb notare are the recorded source of this word family, so the Latin entries below are its direct ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 nota 与动词 notare 是这个词族有记录的来源，因此下面的拉丁词条是它的直系祖先。

definition_zh: 没有什么；没有东西；无关紧要的事；零
definition_en: not anything at all; something too small to matter; and a score of zero in a game
core_image: 抽屉拉开，里面空空的，只有一层薄灰在光里浮动
scene: 抽屉被整个拉开，里面空空的，只有一层薄灰在光里浮动。The drawer was empty, and there was nothing inside but a layer of dust.
sceneCN: 这里是「没有什么、没有东西」（第 1 个义项：一样东西都不存在），句意为抽屉是空的，里面除了一层灰什么也没有。图中可辨识物件：拉开的抽屉、薄灰、窗光。

derivatives.zh: 由 nothing 加 -ness（性质、状态）构成，义为「虚无；空无」
由 good for nothing 固定成词，义为「无用的人」

senses.title: Not anything at all
senses.definition: not a single thing, used when absolutely nothing exists, happens or is present
senses.definitionCN: 一样东西也没有，用于表示完全不存在、不发生或不在场
senses.example: The drawer was empty, and there was nothing inside but a layer of dust.
senses.exampleCN: 抽屉是空的，里面除了一层灰什么也没有。
senses.why: Old English joined nān, meaning not one, to þing, meaning thing, so the word literally says not one thing and still carries that flat emptiness.
senses.whyCN: 古英语把表示「一个也不」的 nān 与表示「东西」的 þing 拼在一起，所以这个词字面上说的是「一样东西也没有」，至今仍带着那种空荡。

senses.title: Something too small or unimportant to matter
senses.titleCN: 无关紧要的事；微不足道的东西
senses.definition: a person or thing of no importance, or a remark or event that matters very little
senses.definitionCN: 不重要的人或事，或价值极小的言论与事件
senses.example: They argued for an hour over nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为一件无关紧要的事争了一个小时。
senses.why: If a thing is nothing, it is not worth counting, so the word easily shifts from absence to worthlessness, especially when people want to dismiss a complaint.
senses.whyCN: 如果一件事是 nothing，就等于不值得计算，于是这个词很容易从「不存在」转到「不值得」，尤其是在人们想打发一句抱怨的时候。

senses.title: A score of zero in a game
senses.definition: zero as a score, especially in sports and games
senses.definitionCN: 比赛或游戏中的零分
senses.example: The match ended three to nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛以三比零结束。
senses.why: A team with no runs has literally scored nothing, so the word for no thing became the name of the zero on the scoreboard.
senses.whyCN: 一支没有得分的队，字面上就是「什么也没得到」，于是表示「无物」的词成了记分牌上那个零的名称。

intro.en: Nothing is a native English compound of a negative word for not one and the noun for thing, and it contracted into a single pronoun in Old English.
intro.cn: nothing 是英语本土的复合词，由一个表示「一个也不」的否定词与表示「东西」的名词组成，在古英语里就已缩合成一个代词。

items.en: Nān was ne plus ān, not one, and it denied even a single item rather than merely denying a quality.
items.cn: nān 是 ne 加 ān，意为「一个也不」，它连单独一样东西都否定，而不只是否定某种性质。

items.en: Þing meant a thing, a matter or an assembly, and it supplied the noun half of the compound.
items.cn: þing 意为东西、事情或议事会，为这个复合词提供了名词那一半。

items.en: The two words were written together as nānþing and behaved as a single pronoun meaning no thing at all.
items.cn: 两个词被写在一起作 nānþing，像一个代词那样使用，意为「一样东西也没有」。

items.en: Middle English respelled the compound with not and thing, matching the shortened negator, and the old nān disappeared from it.
items.cn: 中古英语用 not 与 thing 重拼这个复合词，与缩短的否定词保持一致，旧的 nān 从中消失。

items.en: Modern English keeps nothing as a pronoun and a noun, and fixed phrases such as nothing but and for nothing carry the old emptiness into idiom.
items.cn: 现代英语让 nothing 兼作代词与名词，nothing but、for nothing 这类固定说法把古老的「空」带进了成语。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the other thing-pronouns built on the same pattern; the near-meaning group collects the words English uses for none and zero.
note.cn: 形近组收按同一模式造出的其他 thing 代词；近义组收英语里表示「无」与「零」的词。

entries.definition: A pronoun for any thing at all, built on the same thing element.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「任何东西」的代词，用了同一个 thing 成分。

entries.definition: A pronoun for one unspecified thing, the positive partner of nothing.
entries.definitionCN: 表示某个不指定东西的代词，是 nothing 的肯定对应词。

entries.definition: The noun inside nothing, meaning an object, matter or event.
entries.definitionCN: nothing 里的那个名词，意为物体、事情或事件。

entries.definition: Not one, or not any, used when a quantity is zero.
entries.definitionCN: 一个也不、任何也不，用于数量为零时。

entries.definition: The number that stands for no quantity at all.
entries.definitionCN: 表示完全没有数量的那个数字。

entries.definition: Nothing, especially a zero score in sports and records.
entries.definitionCN: 无，尤指体育与记录中的零分。

normalIntro.en: The word is not one plus thing, and its later senses keep asking what counts as a thing worth having.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「一个也没有」加「东西」，它后来的义项一直在追问：什么才算值得拥有的东西。

normal.en: Nothing is nān plus þing: not one thing, so the word itself explains its own emptiness.
normal.cn: nothing 是 nān 加 þing：一样东西也没有，词本身就把自己的空说清楚了。

normal.en: The same nān is behind no and none, which is why all three refuse a quantity.
normal.cn: 同一个 nān 也藏在 no 与 none 后面，所以这三者都在拒绝某个数量。

normal.en: Middle English respelled the compound with not, linking nothing to the history of not.
normal.cn: 中古英语用 not 重拼这个复合词，把 nothing 与 not 的历史连在一起。

normal.en: Nothing but means only, because everything else has been excluded.
normal.cn: nothing but 意为「只有」，因为其余的一切都被排除掉了。

normal.en: For nothing means either free or wasted, and both say that no payment or result came back.
normal.cn: for nothing 既可以是「免费」，也可以是「白费」，两者都说没有回报或没有结果。

abstract.en: A word made of not one and thing turns absence into a noun, so English can talk about emptiness as if it were an object.
abstract.cn: 一个由「一个也不」和「东西」构成的词，把缺席变成了名词，于是英语能像谈论物件一样谈论空。

abstract.en: When nothing also means unimportant, the language quietly ranks existence by worth.
abstract.cn: 当 nothing 也指「不重要」，语言就在悄悄按价值给存在排位。

abstract.en: On a scoreboard nothing is a number, which shows how easily a word for absence can be counted.
abstract.cn: 在记分牌上 nothing 是一个数字，这说明表示「无」的词多么容易被计数。

examples.en: The drawer was empty, and there was nothing inside but a layer of dust.
examples.cn: 抽屉是空的，里面除了一层灰什么也没有。

examples.en: They argued for an hour over nothing.
examples.cn: 他们为一件无关紧要的事争了一个小时。

examples.en: The match ended three to nothing.
examples.cn: 比赛以三比零结束。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「那辛」——拉开抽屉，里面空空如也，什么也没有；nothing 就是没有什么。

root: 古英语 nān（ne 加 ān，一个也不）与 þing（东西）合成 nānþing，中古英语重拼为 nothing；与 not 同出这一否定词源，英语中没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is not one thing; it then extends to what is not worth counting and to the zero on a scoreboard.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「一样东西也没有」；义项由此扩展到不值得计算的东西，以及记分牌上的零。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open drawer that is completely empty except for a thin layer of dust.
core.cn: 核心意象：拉开的抽屉空空如也，只有一层薄灰。

branches.en: an empty drawer holding only dust
branches.cn: 空抽屉里只有一层灰

branches.en: a hand patting a pocket with no keys in it
branches.cn: 手拍口袋，里面没有钥匙

branches.en: a quarrel over something too small to name
branches.cn: 为一件小得叫不出名字的事争吵

branches.en: a scoreboard still blank after the first half
branches.cn: 半场过后记分牌上仍是空白

branches.en: a team walking off with a zero beside its name
branches.cn: 球队离场，名字旁边是一个零

intro.en: The word joins an Old English negative for not one to the noun for thing, and English built its abstract noun and its dismissive compound on that base.
intro.cn: 这个词把古英语表示「一个也不」的否定词接到表示「东西」的名词上，英语又在这个底座上造出抽象名词和表示轻蔑的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Nothing has no reliable Latin cognate; Latin nihil is built from ne and hilum, not a whit, a different formation, so no Latin entry is listed.
latinIntro.cn: nothing 没有可靠的拉丁同族词；拉丁语用「nihil」表示「无」，它由「ne」与「hilum」（一点点）构成，构词方式不同，因此不列拉丁词条。

definition_zh: 注意到；察觉；通知；告知；告示；通告；短评
definition_en: to become aware of something; also a formal statement that tells people something, a written public sign, and a short review in a newspaper
core_image: 眼睛忽然停在某处细小的地方，心里咯噔一下：我看见了
scene: 雨后的公交站牌下，等车的人无意间抬头，视线落在路对面那件深色外套上。She noticed a small stain on the man's collar as he stood in line.
sceneCN: 这里 notice 是「注意到、察觉」（第 1 个义项：用眼睛或心思捕捉到某个细节）；句意为排队时她注意到前面那人衣领上有一小块污渍。图中可辨识物件：候车的人、路牌、雨后的地面。

collocations.zh: 在很短的通知时间内；临时

derivatives.zh: 由动词 notice 加后缀 -able 构成，义为「容易被注意到的；明显的」
由否定前缀 un- 加 noticed 构成，义为「未被注意到的」
由 noticeable 加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「明显地」

senses.title: To become aware of something
senses.definition: to see, hear or realize something, often without deliberately looking for it
senses.definitionCN: 看见、听见或意识到某事，往往并非刻意寻找
senses.example: She noticed a small stain on his collar.
senses.exampleCN: 她注意到他衣领上有一小块污渍。
senses.why: The Latin source notitia names the state of something being known, so this verb starts from a fact entering your mind rather than from a deliberate search.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 notitia 指「被知道的状态」，所以这个动词的起点是某个事实自己进了心里，而不是刻意去找。

senses.title: A formal statement that tells someone something
senses.definition: an official or formal message or warning given to a person who must act on it
senses.definitionCN: 正式或官方地告知某人的消息、警告，收信人往往要据此行动
senses.example: The tenant received notice that the rent would rise in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 租客收到了房租将在春天上涨的通知。
senses.why: Once notitia means a piece of knowledge, it can also mean handing that knowledge to someone who must respond, which is why the noun turns official.
senses.whyCN: notitia 既然能指「一条已知的消息」，也就能指把这条消息交给需要作出回应的人，于是这个名词带上了正式、官方的色彩。

senses.title: A written sign giving public information
senses.definition: a piece of paper or a sign placed in a public spot to tell people something
senses.definitionCN: 张贴在公共场所、用来告知信息的纸片或牌子
senses.example: A notice on the door said the library would close early.
senses.exampleCN: 门上的一张告示说图书馆会提前关门。
senses.why: A written notice is knowledge fixed on paper, so the same word moves from what is told to what is posted for everyone to read.
senses.whyCN: 书面告示就是把「已知的消息」固定在纸上，同一个词便从「被告知的事」转到「贴出来给所有人看的东西」。

senses.title: A short review of a performance or book
senses.definition: a short newspaper article that judges a play, film or book
senses.definitionCN: 报刊上评价戏剧、电影或书籍的短文
senses.example: The young actor got a favourable notice in the morning paper.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻演员在晨报上得到了一篇好评。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century papers printed such reviews beside announcements, so a word for an announcement came to name a printed judgement of a performance as well.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪的报纸把剧评和各类公告排在一起，于是原本表示「通告」的词也用来指印在报上的演出评价。

intro.en: Notice comes from a Latin noun for being known, travelled through French, and keeps both the act of seeing and the official statement in modern English.
intro.cn: notice 源自拉丁语中表示「被知晓」的名词，经法语传入英语，至今同时保留「看见」与「正式告知」两条线索。

items.en: The verb noscere meant to get to know or to recognise, and it is the root behind a whole family of words about knowledge.
items.cn: 动词 noscere 意为认识、认出，是整族「知识」词汇共同的根。

items.en: Notitia named the state of being known, and could also mean a piece of information or an acquaintance.
items.cn: notitia 指「被知道的状态」，也可指一则消息或一位相识的人。

items.en: Old French kept notice for information, knowledge and a warning, and passed the word into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语保留 notice 一词，表示消息、知识与警告，并在诺曼时期之后把它传入英语。

items.en: In Middle English the word covered both what a person came to know and the formal warning that told people what to do.
items.cn: 在中古英语里，这个词既指一个人得知的事，也指告诉人们该怎么做的正式警告。

items.en: Modern English adds the public written sign and the newspaper review, while the verb stays close to simply seeing something.
items.cn: 现代英语又添上公共场所的书面告示与报刊短评，而动词仍旧贴近「看见了什么」这一层。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same Latin root for knowing; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for perceiving.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「知道」词根上的词；近义组收表示察觉的动词。

entries.definition: An idea or belief held in the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 头脑中持有的一种想法或看法。

entries.definition: Important or unusual enough to deserve attention.
entries.definitionCN: 重要或不寻常到值得留意的。

entries.definition: A system of written signs used in music or mathematics.
entries.definitionCN: 音乐或数学中使用的一套书写符号。

entries.definition: The state of being widely known for something bad.
entries.definitionCN: 因坏事而广为人知的状态。

entries.definition: To become aware of something through the senses.
entries.definitionCN: 通过感官察觉到某事物。

entries.definition: To watch something carefully and take in the details.
entries.definitionCN: 仔细观察并留意细节。

entries.definition: To find something that is hidden or easy to miss.
entries.definitionCN: 发现隐藏或容易漏掉的事物。

entries.definition: To make out something that is not obvious.
entries.definitionCN: 辨认出并不明显的事物。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin root for knowing, and its two halves, seeing and telling, both grow from the same idea of something becoming known.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词长在表示「知道」的拉丁词根上，它的两半——看见与告知——都出自「某事被知道」这同一个念头。

normal.en: Noscere in Latin means to get to know, so notice is what happens when something becomes known to your eyes.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 noscere 意为认识，所以 notice 就是某样东西被你的眼睛知道的那一刻。

normal.en: Notice entered English first as a noun from notitia; the verb came later by using the noun as an action.
normal.cn: notice 先以名词身份从 notitia 进入英语，动词是后来把这个名词当动作来用。

normal.en: Noticeable adds -able to notice, meaning able to be noticed, and the final e stays before the suffix.
normal.cn: noticeable 在 notice 后加 -able，意为「能被注意到的」，词尾的 e 在加后缀时保留。

normal.en: Notify is built differently: notus plus -ify, to make known, so it means telling someone officially rather than merely seeing.
normal.cn: notify 的构造不同：notus 加 -ify，意为「使被知道」，所以它指正式告知某人，而不只是看见。

normal.en: At short notice means with very little warning, because notice here is the time given before something happens.
normal.cn: at short notice 意为几乎没有提前告知，因为这里的 notice 指事情发生前留给你的那段时间。

abstract.en: A notice board holds many small facts pinned in place, each waiting for the one person who needs it.
abstract.cn: 布告栏上钉着许多小事，每一件都在等那个恰好需要它的人。

abstract.en: Seeing and telling are two ends of one thread: what you notice may later have to be announced to others.
abstract.cn: 看见与告知是同一条线的两端：你注意到的事，后来可能要告知别人。

abstract.en: A word that can mean a glance and a resignation letter shows how much weight lies in simply being told.
abstract.cn: 一个词既能指一瞥，又能指辞职信，说明「被告知」这件事本身有多重。

examples.en: She noticed a small stain on his collar.
examples.cn: 她注意到他衣领上有一小块污渍。

examples.en: The staff were given notice of the change in the rota.
examples.cn: 员工们收到了排班变更的通知。

examples.en: A handwritten notice was pinned beside the lift.
examples.cn: 电梯旁钉着一张手写的告示。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诺替事」——答应替人办事，就得时时留意、件件告知；notice 既是留意，也是通知。

root: 一般认为来自拉丁语 notitia（被知道的状态），源于 noscere（认识），经古法语 notice 进入英语；同族词多与「知道、记号」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is something entering your awareness; from there the word splits into the private act of seeing and the public act of telling, with the posted sign and the printed review as its outward forms.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是某样东西进入你的意识；由此分出私下「看见」与公开「告知」两条路，张贴的告示与报刊短评则是它外在的形态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pair of eyes stopping on one small detail while the mind registers it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一双眼睛停在某个细小之处，心里记下了它。

branches.en: a glance that catches a stain on a collar
branches.cn: 一眼瞥见衣领上的污渍

branches.en: a fact moving from one mind to another
branches.cn: 一件事从一个人心里传到另一个人心里

branches.en: a sheet of paper pinned beside a door
branches.cn: 钉在门边的一张纸

branches.en: a letter that warns of a coming change
branches.cn: 预告即将变动的一封信

branches.en: a short column judging a new play
branches.cn: 评价一部新戏的短栏

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin verb for knowing and a Latin noun for being known, then passes through French without carrying an English prefix of its own.
intro.cn: 这个词立在表示「认识」的拉丁动词与表示「被知道」的拉丁名词上，经法语进入英语，本身不带英语前缀。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: to get to know, to recognise

derivatives.zh: 同一词根上的名词，义为「概念；想法」
同一词根上的形容词，义为「值得注意的」

definition_zh: 概念；观念；想法；看法；念头；（复数）小商品
definition_en: an idea, concept, or belief held in the mind, often vague, personal, or whimsical
core_image: 雾里渐渐成形的一团轮廓：你知道它是什么，却还说不清
scene: 一名女子在餐巾纸上画出大概的轮廓，说明她心里设想的那个主意。A woman sketches a rough shape on a napkin to show the notion she has in mind.
sceneCN: 这里 notion 是「心里的概念、想法」（第 1 个义项：一般概念）；句意：一位女士在餐巾纸上粗略画出一个形状，说明她心里的想法。图中可辨识物件：餐巾纸、铅笔、粗略的草图、咖啡杯、桌边的笔记本；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: （复数 notions）小商品；杂货（美式英语）

collocations.zh: 完全不知道；对……毫无概念

derivatives.zh: 小商品；杂货（美式复数名词）

senses.title: A Concept: something known in the mind
senses.titleCN: 概念：心里认识到的东西
senses.definition: a general concept or conception formed in the mind
senses.definitionCN: 在头脑中形成的一般概念或观念
senses.example: The notion of fairness varies from culture to culture.
senses.exampleCN: “公平”这一概念因文化而异。
senses.why: Latin notio is an action noun from noscere 'to come to know'. It names the result of knowing, an idea held in the mind, not a written note.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 notio 是 noscere“认识、得知”的动作名词。它命名的是“认知动作的结果”，即心里持有的观念，而不是写下的“笔记”。

senses.title: A Picture in the Mind: a mental image
senses.definition: a mental image or impression of something, often only roughly defined
senses.definitionCN: 对某物的心理图像或印象，常常只有粗略的轮廓
senses.example: I had only a vague notion of the city before I arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 到达之前，我对这座城市只有一个模糊的印象。
senses.why: Knowing something can begin with a shape rather than a definition. The result of that knowing is a picture with soft edges, which English calls a notion.
senses.whyCN: 认识一件事可以从一个轮廓开始，而不是从定义开始。这种认识的结果是一幅边缘模糊的画面，英语就叫 notion。

senses.title: Awareness: having no notion of something
senses.definition: knowledge or awareness of something, chiefly in the phrase have no notion of
senses.definitionCN: 对某事的了解或意识，主要用于 have no notion of 这一说法
senses.example: He had no notion of how much the repairs would cost.
senses.exampleCN: 他完全不知道修理要花多少钱。
senses.why: If notio is the result of knowing, then having no notion is having no result at all: the mind holds nothing on the matter.
senses.whyCN: 如果 notio 是认知的结果，那么 have no notion 就是完全没有结果：心里对这件事空无一物。

senses.title: An Opinion: a view held as true
senses.definition: an opinion or view, especially one held without full proof
senses.definitionCN: 观点或看法，尤指没有充分证据却仍持有的
senses.example: She rejected the old notion that children should be seen and not heard.
senses.exampleCN: 她否定了“孩子只该被看见、不该被听见”的旧观念。
senses.why: By c.1600 the concept in the mind was treated as a view about the world. The mental result now faces outward as an opinion someone holds.
senses.whyCN: 到 17 世纪早期，心里的概念被当作对世界的看法。这个心理结果转向外部，成了某人持有的观点。

senses.title: A Whim: an inclination with no deep reason
senses.titleCN: 念头：没有多少理由的兴之所至
senses.definition: a whimsical or not very rational inclination to do something
senses.definitionCN: 一时兴起、没有多少理性依据的做事倾向
senses.example: On a whim, he took the notion to paint the door blue.
senses.exampleCN: 他一时兴起，动了把门漆成蓝色的念头。
senses.why: A notion can be an idea that arrives without evidence or plan. From 1746 the word also names such a light, self-generated inclination, close to a whim.
senses.whyCN: notion 可以是一个没有证据、没有计划就冒出来的想法。自 1746 年起，这个词也指这种轻飘飘、自发产生的倾向，接近 whim。

senses.title: An Intention: have a notion to do
senses.definition: an intention or plan, chiefly in the phrase have a notion to do something
senses.definitionCN: 意图或打算，主要用于 「have a notion to do something」 这一说法
senses.example: She had a notion to visit the museum before it closed.
senses.exampleCN: 她打算在博物馆闭馆前去一趟。
senses.why: An inclination that survives long enough becomes an intention. The same mental result now points toward a future action rather than a mere picture.
senses.whyCN: 一种倾向如果持续得够久，就变成打算。同一个心理结果此刻指向未来的行动，而不只是一幅画面。

senses.title: A Vague Belief: I had a notion that
senses.definition: a belief or suspicion held without certainty, often introduced by I had a notion that
senses.definitionCN: 没有把握的信念或猜疑，常由 I had a notion that 引出
senses.example: I had a notion that the keys were still in the car.
senses.exampleCN: 我总觉得钥匙还在车里。
senses.why: The mind's result may be uncertain but still acted on. A notion here is a belief with no firm evidence, the softest form of thinking something is true.
senses.whyCN: 心里的结果可以并不确定，却仍会影响行动。这里的 notion 是没有坚实证据的信念，是“认为某事为真”最柔软的形式。

senses.title: Notions: small goods on a counter
senses.definition: in American English, small useful articles such as thread, pins, and buttons sold in a shop
senses.definitionCN: 美式英语中指针线、别针、纽扣等在商店出售的小件用品
senses.example: The general store kept buttons and thread among its notions.
senses.exampleCN: 这家杂货店把纽扣和线归在小商品里。
senses.why: In 1803 American English used notions for small clever inventions, then for the small goods a dry-goods store sold. The 'bright idea' became a physical trinket.
senses.whyCN: 1803 年美式英语用 notions 指“聪明的小发明”，随后指干货店出售的小商品。“灵光一现的想法”变成了手里的实物小件。

senses.title: The Philosopher's Notion: Cicero's loan translation
senses.titleCN: 哲学家的概念：西塞罗的仿译
senses.definition: in philosophy, a general idea formed by abstraction, especially as Cicero translated Greek ennoia or prolepsis
senses.definitionCN: 哲学中通过抽象形成的一般观念，尤指西塞罗对希腊语 ennoia 或 prolepsis 的仿译
senses.example: The Stoics debated whether a notion could arise before any experience.
senses.exampleCN: 斯多葛派争论概念能否在任何经验之前产生。
senses.why: Cicero needed a Latin word for Greek ennoia 'act of thinking, notion' and prolepsis 'previous notion'. He used notio, the result of noscere, to name an abstract idea in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 西塞罗需要给希腊语 ennoia“思维活动、概念”和 prolepsis“预先形成的概念”找拉丁词。他用了 notio，即 noscere 的结果，来命名心中的抽象观念。

intro.en: Notion comes from Latin notio, an action noun from noscere 'to come to know'. It names the result of knowing, an idea in the mind, and Cicero used it to translate Greek philosophical terms.
intro.cn: notion 来自拉丁语 notio，是 noscere“认识、得知”的动作名词。它命名认知动作的结果，即心中的观念；西塞罗曾用它翻译希腊哲学术语。

items.en: Recorded as nocioun, meaning 'a general concept, conception'.
items.cn: 以 nocioun 的形式记录，意为“一般概念、观念”。

items.en: From Latin notionem (nominative notio) 'concept, conception, idea, notice', an action noun from the past-participle stem of noscere 'come to know'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 notionem（主格 notio）“概念、观念、想法、知悉”，是 noscere“认识、得知”过去分词词干的动作名词。

items.en: Noscere traces to PIE *gno- 'to know', the same family that gives know and knowledge.
items.cn: noscere 可追到原始印欧语 *gno-“知道”，与英语 know、knowledge 同族。

items.en: Cicero formed notio as a loan translation of Greek ennoia 'act of thinking, notion' or prolepsis 'previous notion'.
items.cn: 西塞罗用 notio 仿译希腊语 ennoia“思维活动、概念”或 prolepsis“预先形成的概念”。

items.en: The sense 'opinion, view' is recorded; the modern word now covers both a concept and a stance.
items.cn: 记录到“意见、看法”义；现代这个词同时覆盖“概念”和“立场”。

items.en: The sense 'whim, not very rational inclination' appears in 1746, and American English notions 'small goods' in 1803, by way of 'clever little inventions'.
items.cn: 1746 年出现“念头、不太理性的倾向”义；1803 年美式英语出现 notions“小商品”义，经由“聪明的小发明”这一想法。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound; the second for overlapping meaning, so form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义重叠挑选，使词形与词义分开。

entries.definition: attention or a written announcement. It comes from Latin notitia 'knowledge', a close relative of notio, not from notion itself.
entries.definitionCN: 注意；书面通知。它来自拉丁语 notitia“知悉”，是 notio 的近亲，而不是 notion 的派生词。

entries.definition: a country and its people. It looks close to notion but comes from Latin natio 'birth, race', with no shared root.
entries.definitionCN: 国家与国民。它拼写像 notion，但来自拉丁语 natio“出生、族类”，没有共同词根。

entries.definition: a system of written symbols. It comes from Latin nota 'mark', a different branch from notio.
entries.definitionCN: 符号体系。它来自拉丁语 nota“记号”，与 notio 是不同分支。

entries.definition: the broadest word for something in the mind. Notion is narrower and often suggests something vague or personal.
entries.definitionCN: 表示“心中所想”最宽泛的词。notion 更窄，常暗示模糊或个人的成分。

entries.definition: a general idea formed by abstraction. It is more formal and precise than notion.
entries.definitionCN: 通过抽象形成的一般观念。它比 notion 更正式、更精确。

entries.definition: acceptance that something is true. It is stronger than a notion, which may be little more than a hunch.
entries.definitionCN: 接受某事为真。它比 notion 更强，notion 可能只是一种直觉。

normalIntro.en: Real links only: notio is the result of noscere 'to know', and English notice, notify and notorious belong to the same knowing family.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实联系：notio 是 noscere“知道”的结果，英语 notice、notify、notorious 都属于同一个“认知”词族。

normal.en: Notio is an action noun from noscere 'to come to know': it is the result of knowing, not a written note.
normal.cn: notio 是 noscere“认识”的动作名词：它是认知的结果，不是写下的笔记。

normal.en: Notice, notify and notorious all go back to the same 'know' root, so the not- in notion is a knowing not-.
normal.cn: notice、notify、notorious 都回到同一个“知道”词根，所以 notion 里的 not- 是“认知”的 not-。

normal.en: Have no notion of means the mind holds nothing at all on the subject.
normal.cn: have no notion of 意思是心里对这件事空无一物。

normal.en: A vague notion is an idea whose edges have not been drawn yet.
normal.cn: a vague notion 是边缘还没画清楚的观念。

normal.en: Notions on a shop counter are small goods, a sense that grew out of 'clever little inventions'.
normal.cn: 柜台上的 notions 是小商品，这个义项从“聪明的小发明”长出来。

abstract.en: Picture a shape forming in mist: you can point at it, but you cannot trace its outline.
abstract.cn: 想象雾中渐渐成形的轮廓：你能指向它，却描不出边界。

abstract.en: The same shape can harden into an opinion or soften into a whim.
abstract.cn: 同一团轮廓可以硬化成观点，也可以软化成一时兴起。

abstract.en: Follow it into a shop and it shrinks to a button on a notions counter.
abstract.cn: 跟着它走进商店，它就缩成小商品柜台上一枚纽扣。

examples.en: He had no notion of how difficult the language would be.
examples.cn: 他完全不知道这门语言会有多难。

examples.en: The notion that money brings happiness is widely questioned.
examples.cn: “金钱带来幸福”这一观念受到广泛质疑。

examples.en: The old shop sold needles, ribbons, and other notions.
examples.cn: 那家老店出售针、缎带和其他小商品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诺神」——脑子里“诺”的一声，仿佛神仙递来一个模糊念头 → notion 概念、想法

root: 拉丁语 notio“概念、想法”，是 noscere“认识、得知”的动作名词，追到原始印欧语 *gno-“知道”；notio 是认知动作的结果，不是“笔记”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of notion all name something the mind knows. The knowing can be a concept, a picture, an opinion, a whim, an intention, a hunch, a shop-counter trinket, or a philosopher's abstraction.
sensesIntro.cn: notion 的九个义项都在命名“心里知道的东西”。这种知道可以是概念、画面、看法、一时兴起、打算、直觉、柜台小商品，或哲学家的抽象观念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shape forming in the mind, known before it is clearly defined.
core.cn: 核心意象：心中渐渐成形的轮廓，先被知道，后才有清楚定义。

branches.en: THE KNOWN SHAPE: a general concept, and a mental picture with soft edges.
branches.cn: 被认知的轮廓：一般概念，以及边缘模糊的心理画面。

branches.en: AWARENESS: having a notion, or having no notion at all.
branches.cn: 知晓：有概念，或完全没有概念。

branches.en: VIEW AND BELIEF: an opinion held as true, and a hunch held without certainty.
branches.cn: 看法与信念：自认为真的观点，以及没有把握的直觉。

branches.en: INCLINATION AND INTENTION: a whim that arrives, and a plan that stays.
branches.cn: 倾向与意图：突然到来的念头，以及留下来成为打算的念头。

branches.en: FROM TRINKET TO ABSTRACTION: small shop goods, and Cicero's philosophical concept.
branches.cn: 从小商品到抽象：柜台小货，以及西塞罗的哲学概念。

intro.en: Notion is the Latin noun notio in English form. Its family adds -al, -ly and -ity, while notice, notify and notorious belong to the same noscere 'know' root.
intro.cn: notion 是拉丁语名词 notio 的英语形式。它的词族加 -al、-ly、-ity，而 notice、notify、notorious 属于同一个 noscere“知道”词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin notio 'concept, idea' is an action noun from noscere 'come to know', whose participle notus 'known' also underlies notice and notify. The deepest root is PIE *gno- 'to know'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 notio“概念、想法”是 noscere“认识”的动作名词；其分词 notus“已知的”也支撑着 notice 与 notify。最深层词根是原始印欧语 *gno-“知道”。

items.meaning: a concept or idea in the mind
items.meaningCN: 心中的概念或想法（-ion 构成动作或结果名词）
items.example: The notion of progress is not universal.
items.exampleCN: “进步”这一观念并非普世皆同。

items.meaningCN: 概念上的；理论上的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The cost is notional until the contract is signed.
items.exampleCN: 合同签订前，这项费用只是名义上的。

items.meaningCN: 概念上；名义上（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The two departments are notionally separate.
items.exampleCN: 这两个部门名义上是分开的。

items.meaningCN: 概念性（-ity 构成名词，哲学用语）
items.example: The paper questions the notionality of pure sense data.
items.exampleCN: 这篇论文质疑纯粹感觉材料的概念性。

items.meaning: small useful goods sold in a shop
items.meaningCN: 小商品；杂货（复数形式，美式英语）
items.example: She bought thread and buttons at the notions counter.
items.exampleCN: 她在小商品柜台买了线和纽扣。

items.meaningCN: 注意；通知（同出 notus“已知的”）
items.example: A notice was posted on the door.

items.meaning: to make someone know; to inform
items.meaningCN: 通知；告知（-ify 构成动词）
items.example: Please notify the office of any change.
items.exampleCN: 如有变动，请通知办公室。

items.meaningCN: 通知；告示（-ication 构成名词）
items.example: The app sends a notification when the file is ready.
items.exampleCN: 文件准备好时，应用会发出通知。

items.meaning: well known, usually for something bad
items.meaningCN: 臭名昭著的；众所周知的（-orious 构成形容词）
items.example: The road is notorious for winter accidents.
items.exampleCN: 这条路因冬季事故频发而臭名昭著。

latinEntries.meaning: to come to know, learn, recognize

definition_zh: 小说；长篇小说；新奇的；新颖的；新颁律令（罕用）
definition_en: a long written story about imaginary people and events; also new and unlike anything seen before
core_image: 一本摊开的长篇手稿，纸页很新，故事却是从未有人讲过的
scene: 清晨的旧书店里，店主把一本厚厚的故事书摆到最显眼的位置。She borrowed a novel from the library and read it in two nights.
sceneCN: 这里是「小说、长篇小说」（第 1 个义项：虚构的长篇故事）；句意为她从图书馆借了一本小说，两个晚上就读完了。场景里可辨的物件：旧书架、厚书、昏黄的灯。

derivatives.zh: 由 novel 加表示「从事某事的人」的后缀 -ist 构成，义为「小说家」
由 novel 加名词后缀 -ty 构成，义为「新奇；新鲜事」
由 novelist 加 -ic 构成，义为「小说式的；具有小说特点的」

senses.title: A long work of fiction
senses.definition: a long written story in which the events and characters are imagined rather than real
senses.definitionCN: 篇幅较长、情节与人物皆为虚构的书面故事
senses.example: Her first novel was published when she was twenty.
senses.exampleCN: 她的第一部小说在二十岁时出版。
senses.why: The noun entered English from Italian novella, a short tale, and later grew to mean a full-length invented story.
senses.whyCN: 名词义经意大利语 novella（短篇故事）进入英语，后来指篇幅完整的虚构故事；它和形容词「新」共用同一拉丁词根，因为故事讲的正是没见过的事。

senses.title: New and unlike what came before
senses.definition: new, original and not seen or done before
senses.definitionCN: 新的、独创的、此前未曾见过或做过的
senses.example: They proposed a novel solution to the traffic problem.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为交通问题提出了一个新奇的解决办法。
senses.why: The adjective goes back to Latin novellus, a small form of novus meaning new, so freshness is the oldest layer of the word.
senses.whyCN: 形容词可追到拉丁语 novellus，它是 novus（新的）的小称形式，所以「新鲜」才是这个词最古老的一层意思。

senses.title: A newly issued decree
senses.definition: a new decree or supplementary constitution, especially in civil law
senses.definitionCN: 尤指民法中新增的法令或补充律令，现代英语已罕用
senses.example: The old code was amended by a series of novels.
senses.exampleCN: 旧法典经一系列新颁律令得到修订。
senses.why: In civil law the plural novels named the new constitutions added after the main code, keeping the bare sense of something newly issued.
senses.whyCN: 在民法传统里，复数形式 novels 指编入主法典之后的新律令，保留了「新颁之物」的字面意思；这个义项今天基本只出现在法律史里。

intro.en: Novel runs on two rails from the same Latin root: an adjective for what is new, and a noun for an invented story that was itself a novelty.
intro.cn: novel 沿着同一拉丁词根分出两条路：形容词指「新的」，名词指虚构故事，而这类故事在当时本身就是新鲜事物。

items.en: Novus meant new, fresh or recent, and it stands behind a large family of words about novelty.
items.cn: novus 意为新的、新鲜的、刚出现的，是表示「新」的一大族词的共同词根。

items.en: Novellus was a diminutive of novus, literally newish or young, and it passed into several Romance languages.
items.cn: novellus 是 novus 的小称，字面意思是「较新的、年轻的」，它进入了多种罗曼语。

items.en: Old French novel meant new or fresh, and English took the adjective with that plain sense.
items.cn: 古法语 novel 意为新的、新鲜的，英语借入的形容词就带着这层朴素的意思。

items.en: Italian novella named a short tale, and through French nouvelle it gave English the noun for a story.
items.cn: 意大利语 novella 指短篇故事，经法语 nouvelle 传给英语，成为表示「故事」的名词。

items.en: Modern English keeps the adjective novel for anything strikingly new and the noun novel for a full-length fictional work.
items.cn: 现代英语保留形容词 novel 指「格外新的」，名词 novel 则指篇幅完整的虚构作品。

note.en: The look-alike group collects relatives on the same Latin root; the near-meaning group collects words for stories and for newness.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词根上的同族词，近义组收表示故事与「新」的词。

entries.definitionCN: 新奇的性质，或新奇的小物件。

entries.definition: An account of events, whether real or imagined.
entries.definitionCN: 对事件的叙述，真实的或想象的。

entries.definition: New in design and not copied from anything else.
entries.definitionCN: 设计上新的，不是照搬别处的。

entries.definition: Recently made, arrived or thought of, and therefore new.
entries.definitionCN: 刚做出、刚到达或刚想到的，因而显得新。

normalIntro.en: The root nov means new, and from it grow the novel, the novelty and the person who writes novels.
normalIntro.cn: 词根 nov 表示「新」，小说、新奇与写小说的人都从它长出来。

normal.en: The Latin root nov means new, which is why a novel idea is simply a new idea.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根 nov 表示「新」，所以 a novel idea 就是一个新想法。

normal.en: Novelty adds -ty to the same stem and turns new into a noun: the state of being new.
normal.cn: novelty 在同一词干后加 -ty，把「新」变成名词，指「新奇」这种状态。

normal.en: Novelist adds -ist, the suffix for a person, so it names the one who writes a novel.
normal.cn: novelist 加的是表示人的后缀 -ist，因此指写小说的人。

normal.en: Italian novella, a short tale, is the ancestor of the noun, which is why the two senses look unrelated.
normal.cn: 意大利语 novella 意为短篇故事，是名词义的祖先，所以两个义项看起来像是毫无关系。

normal.en: The adjective takes more novel and most novel, not noveler, because it is a longer adjective.
normal.cn: 形容词的比较级说 more novel、most novel，而不是 noveler，因为它属于较长的形容词。

abstract.en: A story and a new thing share one root because every story is, in a small way, something that did not exist before.
abstract.cn: 故事和新事物共用一个词根，因为每个故事在某种意义上都是过去不存在的东西。

abstract.en: Reading a novel means being handed a world that someone invented, so freshness lives inside the fictional sense too.
abstract.cn: 读一本小说，就是接过一个别人造出来的世界，所以「新」也活在虚构的那个义项里。

abstract.en: The word keeps two doors open: one leads to invention and one to novelty, and both open on the same Latin room.
abstract.cn: 这个词留着两扇门：一扇通向虚构，一扇通向新奇，而它们开在同一间拉丁语的屋子里。

examples.en: They proposed a novel solution to the traffic problem.

examples.en: He writes novels about life in small mountain villages.
examples.cn: 他写关于山区小村生活的小说。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「闹窝」——书里的故事闹成一窝，让人读到深夜；记住 novel 是小说。

root: 拉丁语 novus（新的）→ 小称 novellus（较新的）→ 形容词经古法语 novel 进入英语；名词义经意大利语 novella（短篇故事）与法语 nouvelle 而来。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the Latin root for new; one branch names an invented long story, another describes anything strikingly fresh, and a third survives only in legal history.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是拉丁语表示「新」的词根；一条分支指虚构的长篇故事，一条形容格外新鲜的事物，第三条只留在法律史里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a freshly written manuscript holding a story that nobody has told before.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠刚写就的手稿，里面装着无人讲过的故事。

branches.en: a thick book left open on a night table
branches.cn: 床头摊开的一本厚书

branches.en: a reader refusing to close the last page
branches.cn: 读者舍不得合上最后一页

branches.en: a designer sketching a route no map has shown
branches.cn: 设计师画出一条地图上没有的路线

branches.en: a crowd hearing a proposal that breaks the old pattern

branches.en: a clerk copying a new decree into the law book
branches.cn: 书记员把新律令抄进法典

intro.cn: 这个词立在表示「新」的拉丁词根、它的形容词与小称之上，再由两个英语后缀造出「写的人」与「新的性质」。

latinIntro.en: Latin novus and its small form novellus supply the whole family, from the adjective novel to the noun novelty.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 novus 及其小称 novellus 支撑起整族词，从形容词 novel 到名词 novelty。
