definition_zh: 现今；如今；当今；眼下
definition_en: at the present time, especially when the present is set against the past
core_image: 一张旧照片和一张新照片并排摆着，同一条街已经换了模样
scene: 老人在巷口翻出旧相片，指着同一处街角说当年的店铺早就不在了。Nowadays the street is full of coffee shops instead of grocery stores.
sceneCN: 这里是「现今、如今」（第 1 个义项：指当下的时间）；句意为如今这条街上全是咖啡馆，不再是杂货店。旧照与新街并置，让这个词的时间感更清楚。

derivatives.zh: 由 now 与 day 缩合而来的形容词，多见于旧用法，义为「现今的」
nowadays 的构词基干之一，源自古英语 nu，义为「现在」

senses.title: At the present time
senses.definition: at the present time, in the period we are living in now
senses.definitionCN: 在我们正生活的当下这个时期
senses.example: Nowadays most people carry a phone everywhere.
senses.exampleCN: 如今大多数人走到哪里都带着手机。
senses.why: The phrase behind the word literally meant now on days, so its first job is simply to place an action in the present.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的短语字面上就是「如今在这些日子里」，所以它最基本的工作是把动作安放在当下。

senses.title: The present seen against the past
senses.definition: used to point out how things differ between the present and an earlier time
senses.definitionCN: 用来指出现在与从前之间的差别
senses.example: Nowadays we order food online, but my grandmother still walks to the market.
senses.exampleCN: 如今我们在网上点菜，可我祖母还是走去菜市场。
senses.why: Because the phrase grew out of a comparison between days, the word naturally carries a before-and-after frame.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语本就诞生于「日子与日子」的对照，所以这个词天然带着「前后之别」的框架。

senses.title: Of the present period, placed before a noun
senses.titleCN: 时下的；当今的（口语用法）
senses.definition: placed before a noun in informal speech to mean belonging to the present period
senses.definitionCN: 口语中放在名词前，表示属于当下这个时期的
senses.example: Nowadays children learn to swipe a screen before they learn to write.
senses.exampleCN: 现在的孩子先学会滑屏幕，再学会写字。
senses.why: Once the adverb is felt as a label for the current era, speakers begin to use it as a modifier of the people and things that belong to that era.
senses.whyCN: 当这个副词被当成「当下时代」的标签，说话人就开始把它放到名词前，修饰属于这个时代的人与物。

intro.en: Nowadays began as a spoken phrase rather than a single word: now on days, which English later squeezed into one adverb.
intro.cn: nowadays 起初是一个口语短语而不是单词：now on days，后来英语把它压缩成一个副词。

items.en: The two halves are old: nu meant now, and dæg meant day.
items.cn: 两半都很古老：nu 意为「现在」，dæg 意为「日子」。

items.en: Middle English joined them in the phrase now a dayes, literally now on days, with a as a worn-down form of on.
items.cn: 中古英语把它们连成 now a dayes，字面是「如今在这些日子里」，其中的 a 是 on 的弱化形式。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the phrase was written as one word, and the old preposition had disappeared from hearing.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个短语被写成一个词，旧的介词在听感上已经消失。

items.en: Dictionaries of the eighteenth century list it as a settled adverb of present time.
items.cn: 十八世纪的词典已把它收作表示现在时间的固定副词。

items.en: Modern English uses it mainly in writing and in contrastive statements about how things have changed.
items.cn: 现代英语主要在书面语里、以及在说明事物如何变化的今昔对比句中使用。

note.en: The look-alike group collects short time words built from the same demonstrative parts; the near-meaning group collects other ways of saying now.
note.cn: 形近组收由同一批指示词构成的短小时间词，近义组收其他表示「现在」的说法。

entries.definition: At this moment or at the present time.
entries.definitionCN: 此刻或现在。

entries.definition: On this present day.
entries.definitionCN: 在今天这一天。

entries.definition: In or to no place.
entries.definitionCN: 不在任何地方；无处。

entries.definition: Sometimes, but not often.
entries.definitionCN: 有时，但不常。

entries.definition: At the present time, common in neutral and formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 目前，常见于中性或正式书面语。

entries.definition: In the present period, especially in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 在当前这段时期，多用于口语。

entries.definition: At this time, or soon, depending on the sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 现时，或视句子指「不久」。

normalIntro.en: Split the word into now, a and dayes and it says now on these days, which is simply the present.
normalIntro.cn: 把词拆成 now、a、dayes 三段，意思就是「在这些日子里」，也就是现在。

normal.en: Nowadays hides the words now and day inside it, and together they mean now on these days.
normal.cn: nowadays 里藏着 now 与 day，合起来就是「如今在这些日子里」。

normal.en: The a in the middle is a worn-down on, so the phrase once read as now on days.
normal.cn: 中间那个 a 是弱化掉的 on，所以这个短语原本读作 now on days。

normal.en: The final -s is the plural of day, which is why the word points to a stretch of days rather than one date.
normal.cn: 末尾的 -s 是 day 的复数，所以这个词指的是一段日子，而不是某一天。

normal.en: Nowadays is an adverb, so in careful writing it modifies a whole clause rather than standing before a noun.
normal.cn: nowadays 是副词，在严谨的写作里它修饰整个句子，而不是站在名词前面。

normal.en: Its closest short synonym in speech is these days, which carries the same contrast with the past.
normal.cn: 口语里它最贴近的短说法是 these days，同样带着与过去对照的意味。

abstract.en: The word is a fossil of a phrase: a whole remark about days was squeezed until it fit into one slot.
abstract.cn: 这个词是一个短语的化石：一句关于日子的话被压缩到只占一个位置。

abstract.en: Hearing nowadays always implies a before, because a contrast with the past is built into its bones.
abstract.cn: 听到 nowadays 总会预设一个「从前」，因为与过去的对照已经长在它的骨架里。

abstract.en: It measures time the way a photograph does: it does not give the clock, only the fact that the picture has changed.
abstract.cn: 它衡量时间的方式像一张照片：它不报钟点，只说明画面已经变了。

examples.en: Nowadays most people carry a phone everywhere.
examples.cn: 如今大多数人走到哪里都带着手机。

examples.en: Nowadays we order food online, but my grandmother still walks to the market.
examples.cn: 如今我们在网上点菜，可我祖母还是走去菜市场。

examples.en: Children nowadays learn to swipe a screen before they learn to write.
examples.cn: 现在的孩子先学会滑屏幕，再学会写字。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「闹啊得死」——如今的日子闹得人直喊要死；记住 nowadays 是现今。

root: 由 now（现在）、a（即 on）、day 的复数 dayes 合成的短语 now a dayes，十六世纪写成一个词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is present time; the senses divide into plain time reference, contrast with the past, and an informal attributive use.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「当下的时间」；义项分成单纯的时间定位、与从前的对照，以及口语里放在名词前的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old photograph and a new one of the same street, side by side.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一条街的旧照与新照并排摆着。

branches.en: a phone in every hand on a morning train
branches.cn: 早晨地铁里人人手中的手机

branches.en: a shop staying open late because customers now order at night
branches.cn: 因为客人改在夜里下单而开到很晚的店

branches.en: an old photograph held beside the same street today
branches.cn: 旧照片与今天的同一条街并排

branches.en: a grandmother still walking to the market
branches.cn: 仍然走去菜市场的祖母

branches.en: children swiping a screen before they can write
branches.cn: 还没会写字就先会滑屏幕的孩子

intro.en: The word is a fusion of now, a reduced on, and the plural of day; there is no Latin root, only old words that point at time.
intro.cn: 这个词由 now、弱化的 on 与 day 的复数三块拼成，没有拉丁词根，靠指示时间的旧词组成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaningCN: 介词 on 的弱化形式

definition_zh: 无处；没有地方；毫无进展；偏远之地；远不及
definition_en: in or to no place at all; also used of a remote place and of a complete lack of progress
core_image: 一张地图上所有道路都走到尽头，前方再没有可以落脚的地方
scene: 夜里车在荒原上抛了锚，四周只有风声和黑黢黢的草。After two hours of walking, they found themselves nowhere near the village.
sceneCN: 这里是「远不及、离……还很远」（第 4 个义项：nowhere near 表示差得很远）；句意为走了两个小时，他们离村子还远得很。荒原与抛锚的车把「没有地方」的字面感先立了起来。

pos.zh: 偏远的地方（多见于 the middle of nowhere）

derivatives.zh: 由 nowhere 与 -ville 拼合的口语造词，指偏远又乏味的地方
由 nowhere 与 near 构成的固定搭配，义为「远不及」

senses.title: In or to no place
senses.definition: in or to no place at all
senses.definitionCN: 在任何地方都不存在，或不到任何地方
senses.example: The keys were nowhere in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 钥匙在房间里哪儿都找不到。
senses.why: The word simply fused no with where, so it negates place itself: no location answers the question.
senses.whyCN: 这个词就是把 no 与 where 直接焊在一起，否定的是地点本身：没有任何一个位置能回答「在哪里」。

senses.title: To make no progress
senses.definition: to fail to make any progress or reach any result
senses.definitionCN: 没能取得任何进展或结果
senses.example: Arguing with him gets you nowhere.
senses.exampleCN: 和他争辩毫无用处。
senses.why: If the destination is no place, movement toward it can only end without arrival, which is how the word came to mean no result.
senses.whyCN: 既然目的地是「没有地方」，朝它走就永远到不了，于是这个词引申为「没有结果」。

senses.title: A remote and empty place
senses.definition: a place far from towns and hard to reach
senses.definitionCN: 远离城镇、难以抵达的地方
senses.example: They built a cabin in the middle of nowhere.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在荒郊野外盖了一间小木屋。
senses.why: When a location is so far out that it feels like no place at all, the negated word becomes a name for remoteness itself.
senses.whyCN: 当某个地方远得像是「根本不存在」时，这个否定词就反过来成了「偏远」的代称。

senses.title: Far from reaching a standard
senses.definition: used before near or close to say that something is far from a target
senses.definitionCN: 用在 near 或 close 前，表示离目标差得很远
senses.example: The project is nowhere near finished.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目离完工还差得远。
senses.why: The same spatial gap that produced no place is reused as a gap in degree, so distance in space turns into distance from a standard.
senses.whyCN: 造出「没有地方」的那个空间落差被挪来表示程度差距：空间的距离变成了与标准的距离。

intro.en: Nowhere is a compound of two Old English words, na and hwaer, and it has kept its literal shape for centuries.
intro.cn: nowhere 由两个古英语词 na 与 hwaer 复合而成，几个世纪以来一直保持着字面的构造。

items.en: Na was the plain negative word, meaning no or not any.
items.cn: na 是朴素的否定词，意为「没有、一点也不」。

items.en: Hwaer was the question word for place, the ancestor of where.
items.cn: hwaer 是询问地点的疑问词，是 where 的祖先。

items.en: Middle English wrote the compound as nawher or nowher, still spelling out both halves.
items.cn: 中古英语把这个复合词写作 nawher 或 nowher，两半仍看得清楚。

items.en: Early modern printers settled on nowhere, and the word also began to name remote places.
items.cn: 近代早期的印刷者把拼写固定为 nowhere，这个词也开始用来指偏远之地。

items.en: Modern English adds the figurative senses of no result and far from a standard, as in get nowhere and nowhere near.
items.cn: 现代英语再加上「没有结果」与「远不及」两个比喻义，如 get nowhere 与 nowhere near。

note.en: The look-alike group collects place adverbs built on where; the near-meaning group collects words for remoteness and for useless effort.
note.cn: 形近组收由 where 构成的同族地点副词，近义组收表示偏远与徒劳的词。

entries.definition: In or to a place that is not named.
entries.definitionCN: 在或到某个未指明的地方。

entries.definition: In or to any place at all.
entries.definitionCN: 在任何地方。

entries.definition: In or to all places.
entries.definitionCN: 到处；各处。

entries.definition: In or to another place.
entries.definitionCN: 在或到别处。

entries.definition: Far away from towns and people.
entries.definitionCN: 远离城镇与人群的。

entries.definition: Cut off from others and hard to reach.
entries.definitionCN: 与外界隔绝、难以抵达的。

entries.definition: In a way that produces no result.
entries.definitionCN: 以毫无结果的方式。

entries.definition: A wild area with no towns or roads.
entries.definitionCN: 没有城镇与道路的荒野。

normalIntro.en: No plus where spells out no place; from that blank the word grows the senses of no result and far from a mark.
normalIntro.cn: no 与 where 一拼就写出「没有地方」；从这个空白里又长出「没有结果」与「差得远」。

normal.en: Nowhere is no plus where, so its literal meaning is not any place.
normal.cn: nowhere 就是 no 加 where，字面意思是不在任何地方。

normal.en: Because the destination is no place, get nowhere means you never arrive at a result.
normal.cn: 因为终点就是「没有地方」，所以 get nowhere 指永远到不了结果。

normal.en: Nowhere near keeps the same gap but measures distance from a target, not from a town.
normal.cn: nowhere near 保留同一个落差，只是量的是与目标的距离，而不是与城镇的距离。

normal.en: The middle of nowhere turns the negative into a name for the emptiest place around.
normal.cn: the middle of nowhere 把这个否定词反过来当成最空旷之处的名字。

normal.en: Spell it as one word: there is no space between no and where.
normal.cn: 拼写时写成一个词，no 与 where 之间不留空格。

abstract.en: A road ends in open grass: every direction has been walked and none leads anywhere.
abstract.cn: 一条路在荒草里到头：每个方向都走过了，哪儿也去不了。

abstract.en: Nowhere is the map's way of drawing an absence, a blank where a name should be.
abstract.cn: nowhere 是地图画「空缺」的方式：本该写名字的地方留了一片空白。

abstract.en: The same word can lose a place and lose a result, because both are destinations that never arrive.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能失去地点，也能失去结果，因为两者都是永远抵达不了的终点。

examples.en: The keys were nowhere in the room.
examples.cn: 钥匙在房间里哪儿都找不到。

examples.en: Arguing with him gets you nowhere.
examples.cn: 和他争辩毫无用处。

examples.en: The project is nowhere near finished.
examples.cn: 这个项目离完工还差得远。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「闹胃」——找不到地方吃饭，胃里闹得慌；记住 nowhere 是无处。

root: 古英语 na（不）与 hwær（何处）复合，字面即「何处都没有」；同族词为 somewhere、anywhere、everywhere。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the absence of a place; the senses move from literal no place to no progress, a remote spot, and a gap in degree.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「没有地点」；义项先落在空间上的无处，再引申为没有进展、偏远之地，以及程度上的远不及。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a road that runs out at the edge of open grass, with no name on the map.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条路在荒草边缘走到尽头，地图上也没有名字。

branches.en: keys missing from every drawer in the room
branches.cn: 钥匙翻遍房间每个抽屉都不见

branches.en: a map with a blank space where a village should be
branches.cn: 本该标着村庄的地图却是一片空白

branches.en: two people arguing until both are tired
branches.cn: 两个人争到都累了也没个结果

branches.en: a cabin standing alone beyond the last road
branches.cn: 最后一道路尽头之外孤零零的小屋

branches.en: an unfinished bridge far from the plan
branches.cn: 与图纸相去甚远的半截桥

intro.en: The word is built from the Old English negative na and the question word hwaer; it has no Latin root, and its family is a row of place adverbs.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语的否定词 na 与疑问词 hwær 组成，没有拉丁词根，同族是一整排地点副词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: place, as in somewhere or anywhere

definition_zh: 核的；原子核的；核能的；细胞核的
definition_en: relating to a nucleus, especially the atomic nucleus or the cell nucleus
core_image: 一个极小的中心，周围绕着一圈电子或一层膜
scene: 这个国家大部分电力来自核电站。The country gets most of its electricity from nuclear power plants.
sceneCN: 这里 nuclear 指「核能的」（第 2 个义项：由原子核反应释放能量的）；句意：该国大部分电力来自核电站；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 核的；原子核的；核能的；核武器的；细胞核的；核心家庭的

senses.title: Of the atomic nucleus
senses.definition: relating to the nucleus of an atom
senses.definitionCN: 与原子核有关的
senses.example: Nuclear size is measured in femtometres.
senses.exampleCN: 原子核的尺度以飞米计。
senses.why: The adjective simply attaches the noun nucleus to atomic physics, where the centre of the atom is the object of study.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把 nucleus 直接接到原子物理上，那里研究的对象就是原子的中心。

senses.title: Nuclear energy
senses.definition: describing energy released by changes in atomic nuclei
senses.definitionCN: 指由原子核变化释放的能量
senses.example: Nuclear power supplies a fifth of the country's electricity.
senses.exampleCN: 核电供应全国五分之一的电力。
senses.why: Because the energy comes from the nucleus rather than from chemical bonds, the adjective names the source of the power.
senses.whyCN: 因为能量来自原子核而不是化学键，这个形容词命名的就是能量的来源。

senses.title: Nuclear weapons
senses.definition: describing weapons whose explosive force comes from nuclear reactions
senses.definitionCN: 指爆炸力来自核反应的武器
senses.example: The treaty limits the number of nuclear warheads.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约限制核弹头的数量。
senses.why: The same source of energy, released deliberately and instantly, yields a weapon, so the adjective marks the mechanism of the blast.
senses.whyCN: 同一种能量来源若被有意瞬间释放，就成为武器，因此这个形容词标出爆炸的机制。

senses.title: Nuclear physics
senses.definition: relating to the branch of physics that studies nuclei and their reactions
senses.definitionCN: 与研究核及其反应的物理分支有关
senses.example: Nuclear physics grew out of radioactivity research.
senses.exampleCN: 核物理学从放射性研究中发展出来。
senses.why: A discipline named after its object takes the adjective as a fixed modifier, as in nuclear physics or nuclear chemistry.
senses.whyCN: 以研究对象命名的学科会把形容词作为固定修饰语，如 nuclear physics 或 nuclear chemistry。

senses.title: Of the cell nucleus
senses.definition: relating to the nucleus of a living cell
senses.definitionCN: 与活细胞的细胞核有关的
senses.example: Nuclear DNA is separated from the cytoplasm by a membrane.
senses.exampleCN: 核 DNA 由一层膜与细胞质隔开。
senses.why: Biology uses the same adjective for the cell's centre, and compounds such as nuclear envelope keep the two senses distinct by context.
senses.whyCN: 生物学用同一个形容词指细胞的中心，nuclear envelope 等复合词靠上下文把两个义项区分开。

senses.title: Nuclear family
senses.definition: describing a household of parents and their dependent children
senses.definitionCN: 指由父母与其未成年子女组成的家庭
senses.example: The survey compared nuclear and extended households.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查比较了核心家庭与大家庭。
senses.why: Social science borrowed the image of a small centre with close members, contrasting it with the wider extended family.
senses.whyCN: 社会科学借用「小核心加紧密成员」的意象，用来与更宽的扩展家庭相对照。

senses.title: Nuclear medicine
senses.definition: describing medical techniques that use radioactive substances
senses.definitionCN: 指使用放射性物质的医学技术
senses.example: Nuclear medicine scans reveal how an organ is working.
senses.exampleCN: 核医学扫描能显示器官的工作状况。
senses.why: Radioactive tracers are read by their nuclear emissions, so the medical branch is named after the physical process.
senses.whyCN: 放射性示踪剂靠其核辐射被读取，因此这个医学分支按物理过程命名。

senses.title: Nuclear envelope
senses.definition: describing the membrane that surrounds the cell nucleus
senses.definitionCN: 指包围细胞核的那层膜
senses.example: The nuclear envelope breaks down during mitosis.
senses.exampleCN: 核膜在有丝分裂过程中解体。
senses.why: An anatomical compound uses the adjective to say which structure the membrane belongs to.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学复合词用这个形容词说明这层膜属于哪个结构。

senses.title: Figurative extreme option
senses.definition: in politics, describing an extreme measure reserved as a last resort
senses.definitionCN: 政治语境中指留作最后手段的极端措施
senses.example: Both sides avoided the nuclear option in the talks.
senses.exampleCN: 双方在谈判中都避免使用极端手段。
senses.why: The destructive power of nuclear weapons supplies a metaphor for any step that would end the game.
senses.whyCN: 核武器的破坏力为任何「一出手就终结局面」的步骤提供了比喻。

intro.en: Nuclear is the adjective of nucleus, formed with -ar; its history splits between atomic physics and cell biology.
intro.cn: nuclear 是 nucleus 的形容词，由 -ar 构成；它的历史分为原子物理与细胞生物学两条线。

items.en: Nucleus, diminutive of nux 'nut', meant a kernel. English borrowed the noun in the 17th century.
items.cn: nucleus 是 nux「坚果」的指小形式，意为果仁。英语在 17 世纪借入这个名词。

items.en: The adjective nuclear is recorded in the 19th century in general senses such as 'relating to a kernel or centre'. The precise first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 形容词 nuclear 在 19 世纪有「与果核或中心有关的」这类一般义。确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Robert Brown's nucleus gave biology its own central body, and nuclear later described the structures around it.
items.cn: Robert Brown 的 nucleus 为生物学提供了自己的中心小体，nuclear 后来用于描述它周围的结构。

items.en: Rutherford's model placed nearly all atomic mass in a tiny nucleus, and nuclear physics was born around 1911 to 1912.
items.cn: 卢瑟福的模型把原子几乎全部质量放进一个极小的核，核物理学约在 1911 至 1912 年诞生。

items.en: The nuclear age fixed the word in public language through weapons and power stations, adding figurative uses such as the nuclear option.
items.cn: 1945 年之后的核时代通过武器与电站把这个词固定进公共语言，并增加了「极端手段」这类比喻用法。

note.en: The first group separates nuclear from the noun and from near-looking words; the second separates its atomic sense from its biological and social senses.
note.cn: 第一组把 nuclear 与名词及形近词分开；第二组把它的原子义与生物、社会义分开。

entries.definition: The central body itself; nuclear is the adjective used in nuclear power, nuclear physics or nuclear envelope.
entries.definitionCN: 指中心小体本身；nuclear 是用于 nuclear power、nuclear physics、nuclear envelope 的形容词。

entries.definition: A structure inside the cell nucleus, not the nucleus; it is a noun and never replaces nuclear as a modifier.
entries.definitionCN: 指细胞核内的一个结构，不是细胞核本身；它是名词，不能像 nuclear 那样作修饰语。

entries.definition: Used almost only in nucleic acid; it refers to the chemistry of nuclei, not to nuclear energy.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎只用于 nucleic acid；它指核的化学，而不是核能。

entries.definition: Relating to atoms as wholes; atomic energy can mean energy from the atom generally, while nuclear pins it to the nucleus.
entries.definitionCN: 指与整个原子有关的；atomic energy 可泛指原子能，而 nuclear 明确限定在原子核。

entries.definition: Describing unstable nuclei that emit radiation; a material can be radioactive without being part of a nuclear reactor.
entries.definitionCN: 指不稳定的核发出辐射；某种材料可以具有放射性，却与核反应堆无关。

entries.definition: Located at the middle; it is the everyday word for position and never means atomic or cell nuclei.
entries.definitionCN: 指位于中间，是表示位置的日常词，从不指原子核或细胞核。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: nucleus + -ar: the adjective of the kernel.
normal.cn: nucleus + -ar：果核的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs nucleus, nuclear-powered, nuclear-free and nucleonics.
normal.cn: 同族词有 nucleus、nuclear-powered、nuclear-free、nucleonics。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: nuclear power, nuclear weapon, nuclear family, nuclear envelope.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：核能、核武器、核心家庭、核膜。

normal.en: Context decides whether the nucleus is in an atom or in a cell.
normal.cn: 上下文决定这个核是在原子里还是在细胞里。

normal.en: The nuclear option is a metaphor borrowed from the bomb.
normal.cn: nuclear option 是从核弹借来的比喻。

abstract.en: An atom is a tiny sun with a nucleus at the centre and electrons in orbit.
abstract.cn: 原子像一颗微型太阳，原子核在中心，电子在轨道上。

abstract.en: A nuclear family is a small core with a clear boundary, like a nucleus with its membrane.
abstract.cn: 核心家庭像一个有清晰边界的小核心，如同带膜的细胞核。

abstract.en: The nuclear option is the move that ends the game, like a bomb in a board game.
abstract.cn: 极端手段是终结整局棋的那一步，就像棋盘游戏里的炸弹。

examples.en: Nuclear power produces electricity without burning coal.
examples.cn: 核能发电不燃烧煤炭。

examples.en: The nuclear envelope separates the cell's DNA from the cytoplasm.
examples.cn: 核膜把细胞的 DNA 与细胞质隔开。

examples.en: The country expanded its nuclear medicine programme.
examples.cn: 该国扩大了核医学项目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「nucleus（核）+ -ar」→ 跟核有关的 → 原子核的、核能的、细胞核的

root: 拉丁语 nux「坚果」→ nucleus「果仁、小核」→ 英语 nucleus；加形容词后缀 -ar 构成 nuclear。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses divide into three families: atomic physics and its power and weapons, cell biology and its envelope, and social or figurative cores such as the nuclear family and the nuclear option.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项分成三族：原子物理及其能量与武器，细胞生物学及其核膜，以及核心家庭、极端手段这类社会或比喻性的核心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tiny centre with electrons or a membrane wrapped around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个极小的中心，外面绕着一圈电子或一层膜。

branches.en: ATOMIC SCIENCE: the nucleus as an object of study and the discipline built around it.
branches.cn: 原子科学：作为研究对象的原子核，以及围绕它建立的学科。

branches.en: ENERGY AND MEDICINE: power from the nucleus, weapons from the same source, and radioactive tracers.
branches.cn: 能量与医学：来自核的能量，同源的武器，以及放射性示踪剂。

branches.en: CELL BIOLOGY: the nucleus of a living cell and the membrane around it.
branches.cn: 细胞生物学：活细胞的细胞核及其周围的膜。

branches.en: SOCIAL CORE: the small household built around parents and children.
branches.cn: 社会核心：围绕父母与子女建立的小家庭。

branches.en: METAPHOR: the destructive force of the bomb becomes a last-resort political move.
branches.cn: 比喻：核弹的破坏力变成政治上最后才用的手段。

intro.en: Nuclear adds the Latin adjective ending -ar to nucleus; the word then multiplies in compounds.
intro.cn: nuclear 在 nucleus 后加拉丁语形容词词尾 -ar；随后在复合词中大量增殖。

latinIntro.en: Latin nux and nucleus supply the root; -ar comes from Latin -aris. Compounds such as nuclear-powered and nuclear-free are English formations.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nux 与 nucleus 提供词根；-ar 来自拉丁语 -aris。nuclear-powered、nuclear-free 等复合词是英语构造。

items.example: Nuclear reactions change the identity of atoms.
items.exampleCN: 核反应改变原子的身份。

items.example: The nucleus is the cell's control centre.
items.exampleCN: 细胞核是细胞的控制中心。

items.example: A nuclear-powered submarine can stay under for months.
items.exampleCN: 核动力潜艇能在水下停留数月。
该区域被宣布为无核区。
核工程学涵盖反应堆与同位素。
放射性废料需要长期储存。

definition_zh: 麻烦事；令人讨厌的事；讨厌的人；妨害公众的行为
definition_en: something or someone that annoys people or causes trouble; in law, an activity that harms the public
core_image: 一只蚊子贴着耳边打转，整晚的睡意被它一点点搅散
scene: 盛夏的夜里，窗纱破了一个小洞，耳边总有一阵嗡嗡声挥之不去。The constant buzzing became a nuisance that kept the whole family awake.
sceneCN: 这里是「令人讨厌的事、麻烦」（第 1 个义项：带来困扰的事物）；句意为那持续不断的嗡嗡声成了搅得全家睡不着的麻烦。破窗纱与蚊子正是这种小烦扰的来源。

pos.zh: 麻烦事；讨厌的人；妨害公众的行为

derivatives.zh: 由 nuisance 与 call 合成的复合词，指纠缠不休的推销或骚扰电话
由 nuisance 与 tax 合成的复合词，指琐碎而扰人的小额税
由 nuisance 加 -free 构成，义为「没有烦扰的」

senses.title: Something that annoys or troubles
senses.definition: a thing, situation or event that annoys people or causes them trouble
senses.definitionCN: 让人心烦或给人添麻烦的事物、情况或事件
senses.example: The constant buzzing became a nuisance that kept the whole family awake.
senses.exampleCN: 持续不断的嗡嗡声成了搅得全家睡不着的麻烦。
senses.why: Old French nuisance meant harm and annoyance, from a verb for hurting, so the word begins as the discomfort itself rather than the thing causing it.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 nuisance 意为「损害、烦扰」，源自表示「伤害」的动词，所以这个词一开始指的就是那份不舒服，而不是造成它的东西。

senses.title: A person who annoys others
senses.titleCN: 讨厌的人；讨人嫌的家伙
senses.definition: a person whose behaviour annoys other people
senses.definitionCN: 行为让别人厌烦的人
senses.example: He made a nuisance of himself at the party by shouting all evening.
senses.exampleCN: 他在聚会上整晚大喊大叫，很讨人嫌。
senses.why: Once annoyance has a name, that name easily shifts from the feeling to the person who reliably produces it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「烦扰」有了名字，这个名字很容易从那种感受转到总能制造出这种感受的人身上。

senses.title: A legal harm to the public
senses.definition: in law, an activity or condition that interferes with the public comfort or safety
senses.definitionCN: 法律上干扰公众安宁或安全的行为或状态
senses.example: The factory was sued for creating a public nuisance with its smoke.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂因排放烟雾构成妨害公众而被起诉。
senses.why: Because the earliest sense was plain harm, the law kept the word for conduct that harms a whole neighbourhood, not just one person.
senses.whyCN: 因为最早的意思就是「损害」，法律便保留这个词，用来指伤害整个街区而不只是某个人的行为。

intro.en: Nuisance came through French from a Latin verb for harming, and it still carries that original sting.
intro.cn: nuisance 经法语来自一个表示「伤害」的拉丁动词，至今还带着最初的那根刺。

items.en: Nocere meant to hurt or harm, and it is the root behind noxious and innocent as well.
items.cn: nocere 意为伤害、损害，也是 noxious 与 innocent 的共同词根。

items.en: Medieval Latin nocumentum named a harm or an injury done to someone.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 nocumentum 指对他人造成的损害或伤害。

items.en: Old French shortened the family to nuire, the verb for harming or annoying.
items.cn: 古法语把这族词简化为 nuire，即「伤害、烦扰」的动词。

items.en: The noun nuisance meant harm, annoyance and trouble in Old French.
items.cn: 名词 nuisance 在古法语中意为损害、烦扰与麻烦。

items.en: English borrowed it for annoyance of any kind and later gave it a precise legal sense.
items.cn: 英语借来泛指各种烦扰，后来又赋予它精确的法律含义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects relatives on the same Latin root for harm; the near-meaning group collects words for annoyance and for the people who cause it.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「伤害」拉丁词根上的同族词，近义组收表示烦扰以及制造烦扰者的词。

entries.definition: Harmful to health, or strongly unpleasant.
entries.definitionCN: 对健康有害的，或气味强烈令人不快的。

entries.definition: Harmless and unlikely to upset anyone.
entries.definitionCN: 无害的，不太会惹人不安的。

entries.definition: Not guilty of doing anything wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 没有做错事的；无罪的。

entries.definition: Harmful or guilty; now rare.
entries.definitionCN: 有害的或有罪的；现已罕见。

entries.definition: The feeling of being irritated, or something that irritates.
entries.definitionCN: 被惹恼的感受，或惹人恼的事物。

entries.definition: Trouble or effort that is annoying.
entries.definitionCN: 令人烦的麻烦或费劲。

entries.definition: A person or thing that keeps annoying others.
entries.definitionCN: 不断烦扰他人的人或物。

entries.definition: Bothering trouble or a series of small problems.
entries.definitionCN: 恼人的麻烦或一连串小问题。

normalIntro.en: The bone of the word is the Latin verb nocere, to harm, which is why nuisance grew from harm into annoyance and then into a legal wrong.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的骨头是拉丁语动词 nocere（伤害），所以 nuisance 从「损害」长成「烦扰」，再被法律固定成一种侵害。

normal.en: Nuisance and noxious share the Latin verb nocere, which means to harm.
normal.cn: nuisance 与 noxious 共用拉丁动词 nocere，意为伤害。

normal.en: The French noun moved from harm to mere annoyance, which is why the English word sounds milder than its root.
normal.cn: 法语名词从「损害」滑向「烦扰」，所以英语这个词听起来比它的词根温和。

normal.en: Innocent and innocuous add a negative prefix to the same root and turn harmful into harmless.
normal.cn: innocent 与 innocuous 在同一词根前加否定前缀，把「有害」变成「无害」。

normal.en: Public nuisance keeps the legal sense, naming conduct that harms a whole community.
normal.cn: public nuisance 保留法律义，指伤害整个社区的行为。

normal.en: Make a nuisance of oneself is the fixed phrase for a person who keeps bothering others.
normal.cn: make a nuisance of oneself 是固定说法，指不断给别人添烦的人。

abstract.en: A word for harm that softened into annoyance shows how often law and daily speech borrow from each other.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「伤害」的词软化成「烦扰」，正说明法律与日常语言常常互相借用。

abstract.en: Nuisance is small in scale but large in effect: one mosquito can cancel a whole night.
abstract.cn: nuisance 的规模很小，效果却很大：一只蚊子就能毁掉一整夜。

abstract.en: The same root that names poison also names harmlessness, depending on the prefix it wears.
abstract.cn: 给毒物命名的那个词根，也能给无害命名，全看它披着哪块前缀。

examples.en: The constant buzzing became a nuisance that kept the whole family awake.
examples.cn: 持续不断的嗡嗡声成了搅得全家睡不着的麻烦。

examples.en: He made a nuisance of himself at the party by shouting all evening.
examples.cn: 他在聚会上整晚大喊大叫，很讨人嫌。

examples.en: The factory was sued for creating a public nuisance with its smoke.
examples.cn: 这家工厂因排放烟雾构成妨害公众而被起诉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「牛搔死」——牛被蚊子搔得受不了，真是件麻烦事；记住 nuisance 是烦扰。

root: 拉丁语 nocere（伤害）→ 中世纪拉丁语 nocumentum（损害）→ 古法语 nuire（伤害）→ 古法语 nuisance（烦扰）→ 英语 nuisance（讨厌的事、妨害公众）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is causing annoyance; the senses run from an irritating thing to an irritating person and finally to a legal harm to the public.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「造成烦扰」；义项先指烦人的事物，再转到制造烦扰的人，最后落到法律上的妨害公众。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mosquito circling a sleeping ear and undoing a whole night of rest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只蚊子贴着睡觉的耳边打转，把整夜的休息一点点搅散。

branches.en: a mosquito circling one ear in the dark
branches.cn: 黑暗里绕着耳边飞的蚊子

branches.en: a phone buzzing with sales calls at midnight
branches.cn: 半夜被推销电话震得响个不停的手机

branches.en: a neighbour who shouts every evening
branches.cn: 每晚都大喊大叫的邻居

branches.en: a guest who will not stop complaining
branches.cn: 抱怨个不停的客人

branches.en: smoke from a factory drifting over a whole street
branches.cn: 工厂的烟飘过整条街

intro.en: The word stands on a Latin root for harm and travels through a Latin noun, a French verb and a French noun before English gives it a legal sense.
intro.cn: 这个词立在一个表示「伤害」的拉丁词根上，经拉丁名词、法语动词与法语名词一路传下来，再由英语给它添上法律义。

latinIntro.en: Latin nocere and its noun nocumentum supply the core idea of harm, and the related adjective noxius survives inside the English word noxious.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nocere 及其名词 nocumentum 提供了「伤害」这一核心，同族的形容词 noxius 还留在英语的 noxious 里。

definition_zh: 数；数字；号码；数量；编号；总计
definition_en: a word or symbol used for counting, a label that identifies something, an amount or total, and the act of counting a group
core_image: 一列整齐的算珠，每一颗都占着一个可以数出来的位置
scene: 深夜的急诊室门口，护士低头核对登记本，把票上的号码念了出来。The clerk read the number on the ticket and called the next patient in.
sceneCN: 这里的 number 是「号码」（第 2 个义项：用来识别身份的编号）；句意为工作人员读出票上的号码，叫下一位病人进来。图中可辨识物件：登记本、排号票、叫号屏。

derivatives.zh: 由 number 加表示「没有」的后缀 -less 构成，义为「数不清的；无数的」
由 number 加 -ing 构成，义为「编号；编号方式」
与拉丁词根 numerus（数）同源，加 -ous 后义为「众多的」

senses.title: A word or symbol used for counting
senses.definition: a word or written sign, such as three or seven, used to count things or to show an amount
senses.definitionCN: 用来计数或表示数量的词或书写符号，例如「三」或「七」
senses.example: Write the number seven at the top of the page.
senses.exampleCN: 把数字七写在页面顶端。
senses.why: The Latin noun numerus named a count, and English kept the idea of a unit you can point at, so the sign for a count and the count itself share one name.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词 numerus 指「数目」，英语保留了「可以被指认的一个计数单位」这个想法，因此表示数目的符号与数目本身共用同一个词。

senses.title: A label that identifies a person or thing
senses.definition: a set of figures or a single figure printed on something so that it can be told apart from others
senses.definitionCN: 印在物品上的一组数字或一个数字，用来把它与别的同类区分开
senses.example: Her phone number changed after she moved.
senses.exampleCN: 搬家之后她的电话号码变了。
senses.why: Once a figure marks a position in a list, it can also mark identity, because a house, a phone or a ticket is known by the figure printed on it.
senses.whyCN: 数字一旦标出某物在名单中的位置，也就能标出身份，因为房子、电话或票据正是靠印在上面的数字被人认出的。

senses.title: The total amount of a group
senses.definition: the total count of people or things, especially when it is measured or compared with another total
senses.definitionCN: 人或物的总数，尤指被计量或与另一个总数作比较时
senses.example: The number of visitors doubled this summer.
senses.exampleCN: 今年夏天游客数量翻了一倍。
senses.why: Counting a whole group produces one total, so English let the word for a count stand for the size of the group itself.
senses.whyCN: 把一整群数完会得到一个总数，于是英语让表示计数的词直接指这一群的大小。

senses.title: One item in a numbered series
senses.definition: a single item in a numbered series, such as a song in a show or an issue of a magazine, named by its position
senses.definitionCN: 按编号排列的序列中的一项，如演出中的一首歌或杂志的一期，用它的位置来称呼
senses.example: She sang the closing number of the show.
senses.exampleCN: 她唱了演出的压轴曲目。
senses.why: A position in a list turns into a name for whatever sits in that position, so performers speak of the next number without naming the song.
senses.whyCN: 名单上的一个位置会变成占据那个位置的事物的名字，所以演员会说「下一号节目」，而不必点出歌名。

senses.title: To amount to a total
senses.definition: to add up to a particular total, or to count a group and find how many there are
senses.definitionCN: 加起来达到某个总数，或把一群数一遍以得出有多少
senses.example: The crowd numbered more than a thousand.
senses.exampleCN: 人群总数超过了一千人。
senses.why: When a count is applied to a whole group, the noun turns into a verb: you number the group and arrive at its total.
senses.whyCN: 当「数」这个动作落到一整群上，名词就转成动词：你把这群数一遍，就得到它的总数。

intro.en: Number comes from Latin numerus, a word for a count, which reached English through Old French and kept both the thing counted and the act of counting.
intro.cn: number 来自拉丁语 numerus，本义是「数目」，经古法语进入英语，同时保留了「被数的东西」和「数这个动作」两重意思。

items.en: Numerus meant a number, a count or a group counted together, and it was the everyday word for arithmetic quantities.
items.cn: numerus 指数目、计数或一起数出的一群，是表示算术数量的常用词。

items.en: The verb numerare meant to count or to enumerate, and it supplied the action behind the English noun.
items.cn: 动词 numerare 意为数、逐一清点，为英语名词提供了「数」这个动作。

items.en: Old French shortened the Latin word to nombre, which named both a figure and a total; English borrowed this form rather than the Latin one.
items.cn: 古法语把拉丁词缩短为 nombre，既指数字也指总数；英语借的是这个形式，而不是拉丁原形。

items.en: Middle English wrote the borrowed word as noumbre or nombre and used it for figures, totals and the numbering of things in order.
items.cn: 中古英语把借来的词写作 noumbre 或 nombre，用来指数目、总数以及按顺序编号。

items.en: Modern English fixed the spelling as number and extended it to phone numbers, house numbers, magazine issues and musical items.
items.cn: 现代英语把拼写固定为 number，并把词义扩展到电话号码、门牌号、杂志期号与演出曲目。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group collects other words for figures, amounts and totals.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干上的词；近义组收其他表示数字、数量与总数的词。

entries.definition: The whole amount reached when everything is added together.

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Latin noun of counting, and its family keeps returning to signs, totals and the act of naming things in order.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示计数的拉丁名词上，同族词反复回到符号、总数以及按顺序点名的动作。

normal.en: Numerus in Latin means a count, so number begins as something you can point at before it becomes an abstract idea.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 numerus 意为数目，所以 number 起初是能用手指数出来的东西，之后才变成抽象概念。

normal.en: Numeral and numerous share the same stem: one names the sign, the other says how many there are.
normal.cn: numeral 与 numerous 共用同一词干：一个指符号，另一个说数量有多少。

normal.en: Enumerate adds en- and -ate to the same stem, literally counting items out one at a time.
normal.cn: enumerate 在同一词干前加 en-、后加 -ate，字面就是一项一项数出来。

normal.en: A phone number or a house number is a count turned into an identity label.
normal.cn: 电话号码或门牌号，是被转成身份标签的计数。

normal.en: In the phrase a number of, the word stops naming a figure and starts meaning a group of things.
normal.cn: 在 a number of 这个词组里，它不再指一个数字，而开始表示一群事物。

abstract.en: A number is a promise that unlike things can still be compared, because it puts them on one scale.
abstract.cn: 数字是一种承诺：彼此不同的事物也能比较，因为它把它们放在同一把尺子上。

abstract.en: That one word covers symbol, total and label shows how counting turns the world into something English can manage.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时覆盖符号、总数与标签，说明计数把世界变成了英语可以打理的东西。

abstract.en: Every number is a position on an endless line, which is why a figure can also name a place in a queue.
abstract.cn: 每个数都是无尽直线上的一个位置，所以一个数字也能指队列中的某个位次。

examples.en: The number of rainy days fell sharply this year.
examples.cn: 今年雨天的数量大幅下降。

examples.en: Please write your membership number on the form.
examples.cn: 请在表格上写下你的会员编号。

examples.en: The volunteers numbered over forty at the end of the day.
examples.cn: 一天结束时，志愿者总数超过了四十人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「那么」——数一数有那么多个，记住 number 就是数目。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a count you can point at; identity labels, group totals, positions in a series and the verb of counting a whole all grow from that unit.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是可以被指认的一个数目；身份标签、群体总数、序列中的位置，以及数整群的动词，都从这个单位长出来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of counting beads, each one sitting in a place that can be counted.
core.cn: 核心意象：一列整齐的算珠，每一颗都占着一个可以数出来的位置。

branches.cn: 孩子指着写下的数字，把它念出声

branches.cn: 在门口把人群一个一个数过去

branches.en: a singer announced as the closing item of the show
branches.cn: 歌手被报幕为压轴曲目

branches.en: a total written at the bottom of a long list
branches.cn: 长名单末尾写下的总数

intro.en: The word is held up by a Latin noun of counting and its verb, passed on through an Old French shortening, then dressed in English suffixes for 'without', 'process' and 'full of'.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示计数的拉丁名词与动词支撑，经古法语的缩短形式传来，再穿上表示「没有」「过程」「充满」的英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin numerus and numerare are recorded directly and supply the stem behind numeral, numerous and enumerate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 numerus 与 numerare 有直接记录，为 numeral、numerous、enumerate 提供了词干。

definition_zh: 许多的；数量众多的；为数不少的
definition_en: existing in large numbers; many in count
core_image: 沙滩上一眼数不完的贝壳一直铺到浪线尽头
scene: 广场上一队接一队的人来登记，志愿者手里的表格翻了一页又一页。Numerous volunteers signed up before noon.

senses.title: A large number of things
senses.definition: a large number of separate countable things
senses.definitionCN: 可单独计数的事物数量很大
senses.example: The shelf holds numerous small boxes.
senses.exampleCN: 架子上放着许多小盒子。
senses.why: Latin numerus meant number and count, and the suffix -osus means full of, so numerous is literally full of number.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 numerus 意为数目与计数，后缀 -osus 意为充满，因此 numerous 字面就是「充满数目」。

senses.title: A great many people
senses.definition: a large body of people
senses.definitionCN: 人数很多的一群人
senses.example: Numerous guests arrived before the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 许多客人在仪式开始前就到了。
senses.why: The adjective is at home with crowds because Latin numerosus described troops as well as things.
senses.whyCN: 这个词与人群天然相合，因为拉丁 numerosus 既描述事物，也描述军队。

senses.title: Many separate occasions
senses.definition: happening on many separate occasions over time
senses.definitionCN: 在时间上分属许多不同场合
senses.example: She raised the point on numerous occasions.
senses.exampleCN: 她在许多场合提出过这一点。
senses.why: Counting moves from objects to events, and the word follows without changing shape.
senses.whyCN: 计数从物件转到事件，这个词的形态不变地跟了过去。

senses.title: Many items spread over an area
senses.titleCN: 散布在广大区域内的许多事物
senses.definition: many separate items scattered across a wide area
senses.definitionCN: 许多独立事物散布在广阔区域内
senses.example: The delta contains numerous islands.
senses.exampleCN: 这片三角洲上有众多岛屿。
senses.why: A map shows the count as spread, and the same adjective covers that view.
senses.whyCN: 地图把数量呈现为散落状态，同一个形容词也能覆盖这种视角。

senses.title: Many supporting details
senses.definition: supplied in great quantity, as notes or examples
senses.definitionCN: 以大量注释或例证的形式提供
senses.example: The paper offers numerous examples of the pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文为这一模式提供了大量例证。
senses.why: In academic prose the word counts evidence rather than objects.
senses.whyCN: 在学术写作中，这个词数的是证据，而不是物件。

senses.title: Many reasons in an argument
senses.definition: many points offered in support of a claim
senses.definitionCN: 为支持某一主张而提出的许多论点
senses.example: There are numerous reasons to postpone the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 推迟投票的理由有很多。
senses.why: Debate turns quantity into weight, and the adjective supplies the quantity.
senses.whyCN: 辩论把数量变成分量，这个形容词负责提供数量。

senses.title: A large sample in research
senses.definition: a large count of cases in a study or survey
senses.definitionCN: 研究或调查中大量案例的计数
senses.example: Numerous trials confirmed the effect.
senses.exampleCN: 大量试验确认了这一效应。
senses.why: Statistics needs a plain word for a big count before any test is run.
senses.whyCN: 统计在运行任何检验之前，需要一个表示大计数的平实词。

senses.title: A formal substitute for many
senses.definition: used in formal writing where a bare many would sound abrupt
senses.definitionCN: 用于正式写作，替下显得突兀的「许多」
senses.example: Numerous factors were considered by the board.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会考虑了诸多因素。
senses.why: Register, not meaning, separates numerous from many in much modern use.
senses.whyCN: 在现代用法中，这个词与「许多」的区别多在语体，而非意义。

intro.en: Numerous is Latin numerosus, full of number, built on numerus plus the suffix -osus. The Latin line is clear; the first English date is only approximate.
intro.cn: numerous 来自拉丁 numerosus「充满数目」，由 numerus 加后缀 -osus 构成。拉丁线索清楚，英语首见年代只是约数。

items.en: Numerus meant a number, a count, and also a rank or division; its deeper origin is usually traced to a root meaning to assign or allot.
items.cn: numerus 指数目、计数，也指等级或队列；更深的来源通常追到一个表示「分配」的词根。

items.en: The suffix -osus means full of or abounding in, so numerosus is literally full of number.
items.cn: 后缀 -osus 意为充满、多有，因此 numerosus 字面就是「充满数目」。

items.en: The adjective described things countable in great quantity, especially troops, examples and occasions.
items.cn: 这个形容词描述可大量计数之物，尤用于军队、例证与场合。

items.en: English took the adjective in the sixteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个形容词，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The word survives mainly in formal writing as a polished substitute for many.
items.cn: 这个词主要活在正式写作中，作为 many 的雅致替身。

items.en: Number, numeral, enumerate and numerator all descend from numerus, while numerous is its adjective.
items.cn: number、numeral、enumerate 与 numerator 都出自 numerus，numerous 则是它的形容词。

note.en: The first group descends from the Latin number word; the second group gives plainer ways of saying a large count.
note.cn: 第一组出自拉丁语「数目」一词；第二组是表示「大量」的更平实说法。

definition_zh: 坚果；果仁；螺母；狂热者；怪人；要点
definition_en: a fruit with a hard shell around an edible kernel, a small threaded metal block used with a bolt, and in informal speech an enthusiast, an odd person or the central point of a matter
core_image: 一枚褐色硬壳裂开，露出里面蜷曲而饱满的果仁
scene: 秋天的院子里，孩子用小石块砸开一枚外壳坚硬的果子，取出里面饱满的仁。He cracked the shell with a stone and ate the fresh nut inside.
sceneCN: 这里的 nut 是「坚果」（第 1 个义项：带硬壳的可食果实）；句意为孩子用石头砸开壳，吃下里面新鲜的果仁。图中可辨识物件：石块、硬壳、果仁。

pos.zh: 坚果；螺母；狂热者；怪人；要点

senses.title: A hard-shelled fruit with an edible kernel
senses.definition: a fruit made of a hard shell around a kernel that can be eaten
senses.definitionCN: 外面是硬壳、里面是可食果仁的果实
senses.example: Squirrels bury nuts before winter.
senses.exampleCN: 松鼠在入冬前把坚果埋起来。
senses.why: The Old English word named the hard-shelled fruit itself, and the picture of a shell protecting a kernel is the oldest layer in this word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语这个词命名的就是带硬壳的果实本身，「壳护着仁」这个画面是这个词最古老的一层。

senses.title: A small metal block with a threaded hole
senses.definition: a small piece of metal with a threaded hole, screwed onto a bolt to hold things together
senses.definitionCN: 带螺纹孔的小金属块，拧在螺栓上把东西固定在一起
senses.example: He turned the nut until the wheel was tight.
senses.exampleCN: 他转动螺母，直到轮子紧固。
senses.why: A nut grips a bolt the way a shell grips its kernel, and English lent that solid enclosing shape to the hardware part.
senses.whyCN: 螺母咬住螺栓，正像硬壳裹住果仁，英语便把这个坚实、包住东西的形状借给了五金零件。

senses.title: An enthusiast, in informal speech
senses.definition: a person who is extremely keen on a particular activity or subject, used informally with a word in front of it
senses.definitionCN: 对某项活动或话题极为痴迷的人，非正式用法中前面常带一个限定词
senses.example: My brother is a computer nut.
senses.exampleCN: 我弟弟是个电脑迷。
senses.why: Someone who loves one thing to the point of obsession can be named by that thing, so computer nut turns the object of love into a name for its lover.
senses.whyCN: 痴迷一样东西到极点的人，可以用那样东西来称呼，于是 computer nut 把所爱之物变成了爱它之人的名字。

senses.title: An odd or eccentric person
senses.definition: a person who behaves strangely or foolishly, used informally and often unkindly
senses.definitionCN: 行为古怪或愚蠢的人，非正式且常带不客气的语气
senses.example: Everyone at the office thought the new neighbour was a nut.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室的人都觉得新来的邻居是个怪人。
senses.why: A hard shell also suggests something shut off from others, so a person whose mind seems sealed against ordinary reason came to be called a nut.
senses.whyCN: 硬壳还暗示「与外界隔绝」，于是脑子像密封起来、不按常理思考的人，就被叫作 nut。

senses.title: The central point of a matter
senses.definition: the central or essential part of an argument, problem or plan
senses.definitionCN: 论点、问题或计划中最关键、最本质的部分
senses.example: The committee spent a week getting to the nut of the dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会花了一周才触及争端的核心。
senses.why: A kernel is the part worth keeping inside the shell, so the nut of a matter is the small core left after the outer detail is stripped away.
senses.whyCN: 果仁是壳里真正值得留下的部分，于是「事情的 nut」就是剥掉外面那些细节后留下的那点核心。

intro.en: Nut is a native English word with Germanic relatives, and it has a direct Latin cognate in nux, so the shell-and-kernel picture behind it is very old.
intro.cn: nut 是英语本土词，在日耳曼语中有同族词，拉丁语也有直接同源词 nux，所以它背后「壳与仁」的画面非常古老。

items.en: Scholars generally reconstruct a root for nut, related to words for pressing or squeezing, though its exact form is uncertain and not accepted by everyone.
items.cn: 学者一般认为存在一个表示坚果的词根，与「压、挤」的词义相关；它的确切形式不确定，也并非人人接受。

items.en: The Germanic form was a strong noun for a hard-shelled fruit, and it kept the same meaning across the northern languages.
items.cn: 日耳曼语形式是一个表示硬壳果实的强变化名词，在北部各语言中意思保持一致。

items.en: Old English hnutu named the fruit and also stood in compounds for nuts of different kinds.
items.cn: 古英语 hnutu 指这类果实，也出现在指不同坚果的复合词里。

items.en: Latin nux named a nut and its kernel, and from it came nucleus, the little kernel at the centre of things.
items.cn: 拉丁语 nux 指坚果及其果仁，由此产生了 nucleus，即事物中心那颗小仁。

items.en: Modern English kept the fruit sense, then added the threaded metal block and the informal meanings of enthusiast and odd person.
items.cn: 现代英语保留果实义，随后加上带螺纹的金属块，以及「迷」与「怪人」这两个非正式义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds and derivatives built on nut; the near-meaning group collects words for seeds and for keen interest.
note.cn: 形近组收由 nut 构成的复合词与派生词；近义组收表示种子以及强烈兴趣的词。

normalIntro.en: Nut is a native word for a shell around a kernel, and English has kept stretching that shell toward hardware, obsession and a person's head.
normalIntro.cn: nut 是表示「壳包着仁」的本土词，英语不断把这层壳的形象伸向五金零件、痴迷以及人的脑子。

normal.en: Old English hnutu and Latin nux are cognates: two branches of one old word for a nut.
normal.cn: 古英语 hnutu 与拉丁语 nux 同源：同一个古老词分出的两支。

normal.en: Nutty adds -y to nut: having the taste of a nut, and later behaving oddly.
normal.cn: nutty 在 nut 后加 -y：有坚果的味道，后来又指举止古怪。

normal.en: A nutshell is the shell holding the kernel, which is why in a nutshell means in the fewest words.
normal.cn: nutshell 是包住果仁的那层壳，所以 in a nutshell 表示「用最少的话说」。

normal.en: Nutcracker joins nut and cracker, a tool that does exactly what its name says.
normal.cn: nutcracker 由 nut 与 cracker 组成，所说的工具正好做名字里的事。

normal.en: A nut and bolt hold metal together because the nut grips the shaft as firmly as a shell grips a kernel.
normal.cn: 螺母与螺栓能把金属固定住，因为螺母咬住螺柱，就像壳咬住仁。

abstract.en: A nut is a promise that something worth keeping is locked inside something ordinary.
abstract.cn: 一枚坚果是一句承诺：值得留下的东西被锁在平常的外壳里。

abstract.en: One word for shell, hardware and a person's mind shows how English trusts shape more than category.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时指外壳、五金件和人的脑子，说明英语更相信形状而不是类别。

abstract.en: The nut of a problem is the part you must reach before anything else can be said.
abstract.cn: 问题的 nut，是你必须先触及、之后才谈得上其他东西的那一部分。

examples.en: Squirrels gather nuts and hide them under the roots of trees.
examples.cn: 松鼠收集坚果，把它们藏在树根下。

examples.en: The mechanic tightened the nut with a long wrench.
examples.cn: 机修工用一把长扳手拧紧螺母。

examples.en: He is a jazz nut who owns hundreds of records.
examples.cn: 他是个爵士乐迷，收藏了数百张唱片。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a hard shell around something worth keeping; hardware, obsession, oddness and the point of an argument all borrow that shell.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是硬壳包着值得保留的东西；五金零件、痴迷、古怪，以及争论的要害都借用了这层壳。

intro.cn: nut 本身不带前缀或后缀；它的同族词靠与 shell、cracker、pea 复合，以及形容词后缀 -y 生长出来。

latinIntro.en: Latin nux and nucleus are recorded and are direct cognates of the English word, which makes this a native word with a visible Latin twin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nux 与 nucleus 有记录，且与英语这个词直接同源，这使一个本土词罕见地拥有可见的拉丁「双胞胎」。

scene: 清晨的库房里，管理员把收到的旧物一件件摆上长桌，登记重量与年份。The curator lifted each object and wrote its weight in a notebook.

senses.title: A thing that can be seen and touched
senses.definition: a solid thing that exists in the physical world and can be seen or handled
senses.definitionCN: 存在于物质世界、能看见或拿在手里的实体
senses.example: A small object rolled under the table and stopped at her feet.
senses.exampleCN: 一个小东西滚到桌下，停在她脚边。
senses.why: Latin objectum names what has been thrown before the eyes, so the physical thing is the first thing this word ever pointed at.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 objectum 指「被抛到眼前的东西」，所以能看见的实物是这个词最初指向的对象。

senses.title: The focus of attention or feeling
senses.definition: a person or thing toward which attention, interest or a feeling is directed
senses.definitionCN: 注意力、兴趣或情感所指向的人或物
senses.example: The old house became the object of every photographer's attention.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老房子成了每个摄影师关注的对象。
senses.why: Once something is thrown before the mind, it can hold the mind there; the physical thing turns into whatever attention is aimed at.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西既然被抛到心里，就能把心思留住；实物于是转成「注意力瞄准的那个东西」。

senses.title: An aim that a plan is meant to reach
senses.definition: the aim that a plan or an action is meant to achieve
senses.definitionCN: 计划或行动想要达到的那一点
senses.example: The committee met with the object of cutting waiting times.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会开会，目的是缩短等候时间。
senses.why: An aim is also something placed in front of you to move toward, so the word shifts from what is looked at to what is worked for.
senses.whyCN: 目标也是放在你前方、要你走过去的东西，于是词义从「被看着的物」转到「为之努力的终点」。

senses.title: The noun that receives a verb's action
senses.definition: in grammar, the noun or pronoun that the action of a verb is done to
senses.definitionCN: 语法上，承受动词动作的名词或代词
senses.example: In the sentence she wrote the letter, the noun letter is the object.
senses.exampleCN: 在「她写了那封信」这句话里，名词 letter 是宾语。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the word because the object is the thing placed before the verb's action, receiving what is done to it.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用这个词，因为宾语正是被放到动词动作前面的东西，承受着被做的动作。

senses.title: To say that you disagree
senses.definition: to say that you do not agree with or approve of something
senses.definitionCN: 表示不同意或不赞成某事
senses.example: Several neighbours objected to the plan for a new car park.
senses.exampleCN: 好几位邻居反对新建停车场的方案。
senses.why: Latin obicere meant to throw something against someone, and an objection is a word thrown back at a proposal; the modern verb keeps that gesture of standing in the way.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 obicere 意为把东西朝某人扔过去，而反对就是把一句话扔回给一个提议；这个现代动词保留了「挡在前面」的动作。

intro.en: Object comes from Latin words for throwing something before or against; the same root splits into a noun for what is placed in view and a verb for speaking against it.
intro.cn: object 来自拉丁语「把东西抛到前面或对着扔」的说法；同一条词根分成两支，一支指摆在眼前的物，一支指对着说的反对。

items.en: Jacere meant to throw or to cast, and it lies under the -ject of many English words.
items.cn: jacere 意为投、掷，它藏在许多英语词的 -ject 一段里。

items.en: Obicere joined ob-, against or in front of, with jacere, so it meant to throw something in someone's way and also to throw a charge against a person.
items.cn: obicere 把表示对着、在前面的 ob- 与 jacere 合起来，意为把东西抛到某人面前，也指对某人提出责难。

items.en: Objectum, the thing thrown before the mind, came to name whatever is presented to thought, and later the target of a feeling or an aim.
items.cn: objectum 指被抛到心里的东西，用来指呈现在思想面前的一切，后来又指情感或目标所指向的靶子。

items.en: Old French took object as something perceived or opposed, and English borrowed it with both a noun and a verb in view.
items.cn: 古法语把这词用作「被感知之物」与「被反对之物」，英语借用时就同时看到了名词与动词两条路。

items.en: Modern English separates the two by stress: the noun keeps the first syllable strong, the verb moves the beat to the end, and grammar adds the sense of a verb's object.
items.cn: 现代英语用重音把两者分开：名词重音在前，动词重音挪到后面；语法上又添出「动词宾语」一义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same -ject stem from jacere; the near-meaning group gathers words for physical things and for speaking against something.
note.cn: 形近组收同一条 jacere 词干上的 -ject 词；近义组收表示实物与出言反对的词。

entries.definitionCN: 出言或行动反对某个计划或想法。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin verb for throwing, so every sense is some version of something placed in front of someone.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词长在表示「投掷」的拉丁动词上，所以每个义项都是「某样东西被放到某人面前」的某种变形。

normal.en: Jacere is Latin for throw, and the -ject in object, project and inject all comes from it.
normal.cn: jacere 在拉丁语里是投掷，object、project、inject 里的 -ject 都出自它。

normal.en: Object and objection share one root, but object names the thing in front of you while objection names the words thrown back.
normal.cn: object 与 objection 同根，但 object 指摆在眼前的物，objection 指扔回去的话。

normal.en: The noun takes the stress on the first syllable and the verb on the second, a split English made to keep the two jobs apart.
normal.cn: 名词把重音放在第一音节，动词放在第二音节，这是英语为了把两件事分开而做的切分。

normal.en: With the object of is a fixed phrase meaning with the aim of, because an object can be a goal.
normal.cn: with the object of 是固定说法，意为以……为目的，因为 object 可以是目标。

normal.en: Object to is followed by a noun or an -ing form, because the preposition to blocks the plain infinitive.
normal.cn: object to 后面接名词或动名词，因为介词 to 挡住了光秃秃的不定式。

abstract.en: Anything you can point at, anything you aim at, and anything you say against a plan are all, in this word, something placed in front of you.
abstract.cn: 你能指着的东西、你瞄准的东西、你对着计划说的话，在这个词里都是「被放到你面前的东西」。

abstract.en: The same root that throws a stone in someone's path also throws a thought before the mind.
abstract.cn: 同一条词根，既把石头扔到别人路上，也把一个念头扔到心里。

abstract.en: A word that names both a pebble and a protest shows how often disagreement begins with simply seeing something in the way.
abstract.cn: 一个既能指小石子、又能指抗议的词，说明不赞同常常始于「看见有东西挡在路上」。

examples.en: A small object rolled under the table and stopped at her feet.
examples.cn: 一个小东西滚到桌下，停在她脚边。

examples.en: Several neighbours objected to the plan for a new car park.
examples.cn: 好几位邻居反对新建停车场的方案。

examples.en: The committee met with the object of cutting waiting times.
examples.cn: 委员会开会，目的是缩短等候时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥不借它」——东西递到眼前偏说不借；object 既是眼前之物，也是出言反对。

root: 一般认为来自拉丁语 objectum（被抛到眼前之物），源于 obicere（对着投掷），由 ob-（对着）加 jacere（投掷）构成，经古法语 object 进入英语；名词与动词重音不同。

sensesIntro.en: The core is something thrown in front of you; from that one gesture come the physical thing, the target of attention, the aim in view, the grammatical receiver and the words spoken against a plan.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被抛到你面前的东西」；同一个动作长出实物、注意力的靶子、眼前的目标、语法上的承受者，以及对着计划说出的话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a solid thing held up before the eyes, and a hand raised to push it away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件实物被托到眼前，随即有一只手把它推回去。

branches.en: a small thing rolling out of sight under a table
branches.cn: 小东西滚到桌下看不见的地方

branches.en: an old house drawing every camera in the street
branches.cn: 一座老房子引来街上所有的镜头

branches.en: a meeting called to shorten the wait at a stop
branches.cn: 为缩短站上等候时间而开的会

branches.en: the noun that takes what the verb does
branches.cn: 承受动词动作的那个名词

branches.en: neighbours standing up to speak against a plan
branches.cn: 邻居们站起来反对一个方案

intro.en: The word is Latin ob- plus jacere, and its English branch grows through endings that turn the stem into a noun of action and an adjective of judgement.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语的 ob- 加 jacere，它的英语分支靠后缀长成表示动作的名词与表示判断的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin jacere, to throw, and its compounds obicere and objectum are the recorded source of this word, whose stem also underlies project and inject.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 jacere（投掷）及其复合词 obicere、objectum 是这个词语有记录的来源，它的词干也支撑着 project 与 inject。

definition_zh: 反对；异议；反对的理由；不赞成
definition_en: the act of saying that you disagree with something, the reason you give for that disagreement, or a formal protest made in a legal process
core_image: 掌心朝前抬起的一只手，把正在推进的事按住
scene: 庭审进行到一半，辩护律师从座位上站起，手里还捏着那页写满批注的证词。The defence lawyer raised an objection before the witness could answer.
sceneCN: 这里 objection 是「正式异议」（第 3 个义项：法律程序中提出的反对）；句意为辩护律师在证人开口之前提出了异议。图中可辨识物件：法庭座位、批注过的证词、抬起的手。

pos.zh: 反对；异议；反对的理由；不赞成

derivatives.zh: objection 的基础词，作动词义为「反对」，作名词义为「物体」
由 object 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -or 构成，义为「反对者」
由 objection 加后缀 -able 构成，义为「令人反感的；可反对的」

senses.title: The act of saying you disagree
senses.definition: the act of expressing disagreement with a plan, an idea or a statement
senses.definitionCN: 对计划、想法或说法表示不赞同的举动
senses.example: Her objection was quiet but it stopped the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 她的反对很轻，却让表决停了下来。
senses.why: Latin objectio names the act of throwing something against, so the word starts with a gesture of resistance rather than with a reason.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 objectio 指「把东西对着扔过去」的动作，所以这个词的起点是抵抗的姿态，而不是一条理由。

senses.title: A reason given for disagreeing
senses.definition: a reason or argument that someone gives to show why something should not be done
senses.definitionCN: 某人给出的、说明为什么不该做某事的理由或论据
senses.example: The main objection was the cost of the new bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 主要的反对理由是这座新桥的造价。
senses.why: A protest thrown at a plan has to carry something with it, and the reason becomes the thing thrown, so the act and its argument come to share one word.
senses.whyCN: 扔向计划的抗议总得带上点东西，那条理由就是被扔出去的东西，于是动作与理由共用了一个词。

senses.title: A formal protest in a legal process
senses.titleCN: 正式异议；法律上的异议
senses.definition: a formal statement of disapproval made during a trial, a hearing or an official procedure
senses.definitionCN: 在庭审、听证或官方程序中正式提出的不赞成
senses.example: The judge overruled the objection and let the witness continue.
senses.exampleCN: 法官驳回异议，让证人继续说下去。
senses.why: In court the gesture is written into procedure, so objectio becomes a fixed move that a lawyer is allowed to make at a set moment.
senses.whyCN: 在法庭上，这个姿态被写进了程序，objectio 于是变成律师可以在特定时刻做出的一个固定动作。

intro.en: Objection is the noun of action behind object: Latin threw something against, and the noun named both the throw and the thing thrown, which is why it can mean the protest and the reason for it.
intro.cn: objection 是 object 背后的动作名词：拉丁语「对着扔」，这个名词既指扔的动作，也指被扔出去的东西，所以它能同时表示抗议与抗议的理由。

items.en: Jacere, to throw, is the source of the -ject stem shared by object, objection and project.
items.cn: jacere 意为投掷，是 object、objection、project 共用的 -ject 词干的来源。

items.en: Obicere meant to throw something in front of someone, and in argument it meant to put a charge or a protest in another person's way.
items.cn: obicere 意为把东西抛到某人面前，在争论里指把一项指责或抗议挡到别人面前。

items.en: Objectio named the act of throwing against and also the words or grounds that were thrown, which is the exact double sense English keeps.
items.cn: objectio 既指「对着扔」的动作，也指被扔出的那些话与理由；英语保留的正是这双重的意思。

items.en: Old French objection carried the word into English law and debate, where a protest had to be stated in a set form.
items.cn: 古法语 objection 把这词带进英语的法律与辩论，那里提出抗议必须按既定格式陈述。

items.en: Modern English keeps the everyday sense of disagreeing, the sense of a stated reason, and the courtroom sense of a formal protest.
items.cn: 现代英语同时保留三种用法：日常的不赞同、说明的理由，以及法庭上的正式异议。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the -ject stem and the family grown from object; the near-meaning group gathers words for complaint and resistance.
note.cn: 形近组沿 -ject 词干与 object 长出的词族；近义组收表示抱怨与抵制的词。

entries.definition: The noun for a thing, and the verb for disagreeing.
entries.definitionCN: 指物体的名词，也指表示反对的动词。

entries.definition: A person who formally opposes something.
entries.definitionCN: 正式反对某事的人；反对者。

entries.definition: Unpleasant, or open to being opposed.
entries.definitionCN: 令人不快或可被反对的。

entries.definition: An aim, or a judgement free of personal bias.
entries.definitionCN: 目标，或不受个人偏见影响的判断。

entries.definition: An object thrown through the air, such as a bullet.
entries.definitionCN: 被抛射出去的物体，如子弹。

entries.definition: A strong public statement that something is wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 公开而强烈地表示某事不对。

entries.definition: A statement that something is unsatisfactory.
entries.definitionCN: 表示某事令人不满的说法。

entries.definition: Disagreement with an official opinion or decision.
entries.definitionCN: 对官方意见或决定的不赞同。

entries.definition: Resistance to a plan, a policy or a group.
entries.definitionCN: 对计划、政策或团体的抵制。

normalIntro.en: The word is the noun of action of object, so it holds both what a person does and what a person has to say.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 object 的动作名词，所以它既装着一个人做出的动作，也装着一个人要说的话。

normal.en: Objection is object plus -ion, and the suffix turns the act of throwing against into a thing that can be raised and answered.
normal.cn: objection 由 object 加 -ion 构成，后缀把「对着扔」的动作变成一个可以提出、也可以被回答的东西。

normal.en: Raise an objection is the standard pairing, because objections are imagined as something lifted up in a meeting.
normal.cn: raise an objection 是最常见的搭配，因为异议被想象成会议里被举起的东西。

normal.en: Have no objection means you do not oppose it, a phrase common in letters and agreements.
normal.cn: have no objection 意为不反对，是信件与协议里的常用说法。

normal.en: In court a lawyer says objection and the judge either sustains it or overrules it, two verbs that show how formal the move is.
normal.cn: 在法庭上律师说 objection，法官或者 sustain，或者 overrule；这两个动词显出这个动作有多正式。

normal.en: Objector is the person, objectionable is the quality, and object is both the thing and the act of disagreeing.
normal.cn: objector 是人，objectionable 是性质，object 既是物，也是出言反对。

abstract.en: An objection is a hand held up in front of a plan that is already moving.
abstract.cn: 异议就是在一件正在推进的事情前面举起的手。

abstract.en: Every objection carries two things at once: the refusal, and the reason that makes the refusal stand.
abstract.cn: 每一条异议都同时带着两样东西：拒绝，以及让拒绝站得住脚的理由。

abstract.en: A word that can be spoken both in a meeting and in a court shows how disagreement borrows procedure to gain weight.
abstract.cn: 一个既能在会议里说、也能在法庭上说的词，说明不赞同要借程序的形式来加分量。

examples.en: Her objection was quiet but it stopped the vote.
examples.cn: 她的反对很轻，却让表决停了下来。

examples.en: The main objection was the cost of the new bridge.
examples.cn: 主要的反对理由是这座新桥的造价。

examples.en: The judge overruled the objection and let the witness continue.
examples.cn: 法官驳回异议，让证人继续说下去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我不借，可申」——不想借就当面申明理由；objection 是反对与异议。

root: 由 object 加名词后缀 -ion 构成；object 一般认为来自拉丁语 objectum，源于 obicere（对着投掷），由 ob-（对着）加 jacere（投掷）构成，经古法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is refusal thrown at something; the senses divide into the act itself, the reason that supports it, and the formal shape it takes in court.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是把拒绝扔向某件事；义项分成动作本身、支撑动作的理由，以及它在法庭上取得的正式形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a palm raised before something that is already moving forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：掌心朝前抬起的一只手，把正在推进的事按住。

branches.en: a quiet voice that stops a vote
branches.cn: 一句轻轻的反对让表决停下

branches.en: the cost of a bridge named as the reason
branches.cn: 把桥的造价说成理由

branches.en: a lawyer standing up in the middle of a question
branches.cn: 律师在提问中途站起来

branches.en: a refusal that only stands once a reason is attached
branches.cn: 只有接上理由才站得住的拒绝

branches.en: the same reason moved from talk into procedure
branches.cn: 同一条理由，从谈话搬进程序

intro.en: The word is a Latin noun of action built on the verb for throwing against, and its English endings give it a person, a quality and a base verb.
intro.cn: 这个词是建立在「对着投掷」动词上的拉丁动作名词，它的英语后缀又给出一个人、一种性质和基础动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin objectio, a throwing against, is the direct recorded ancestor of this noun, and it rests on obicere and jacere.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 objectio（对着扔）是这个名词有记录的直系祖先，它立在 obicere 与 jacere 之上。

definition_zh: 客观的；无偏见的；真实的；目标；目的；物镜；宾格
definition_en: based on facts rather than personal feelings, or a goal that one aims to reach
core_image: 把一件东西摆到灯下，只看见它本身，看不见自己的影子
scene: 裁判盯着屏幕看回放，尽量不带偏见，只按实际发生的情况判。A referee watches a replay on a screen and tries to stay objective, ruling on what actually happened rather than on what the crowd shouts.
sceneCN: 这里 objective 是「客观的、不带偏见的」（第 3 个义项：不受个人情感影响）；句意：裁判看着屏幕上的回放，努力保持客观，只根据实际发生的情况判罚，而不理睬观众的喊叫。图中可辨识物件：回放屏幕、裁判、哨子、边线、观众席；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 客观的；无偏见的；基于事实的
