最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: The Object in the Mind: the 1610s philosophical sense
senses.titleCN: 心中的对象：17 世纪初的哲学义
senses.definition: in 1610s philosophy, existing as perceived or thought, ideal, representative, or phenomenal, as opposed to subjective or formal
senses.definitionCN: 17 世纪初哲学中，指作为被感知或被思考之物而存在的、观念的、表象的、现象的，与 subjective 或 formal 相对
senses.example: In the old debate, pain was called objective when considered as a thought rather than a bodily state.
senses.exampleCN: 在那场古老争论中，痛苦被当作思想而非身体状态来看时，被称为 objective。
senses.why: The word was built from objectum, 'a thing put before the mind'. In the 1610s that thing was still inside the mind, so objective meant 'existing as an object of thought'.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 objectum“被摆到心智面前的东西”构成。17 世纪初，这东西还在心智之内，所以 objective 意为“作为思想对象而存在”。

senses.title: The Real Thing Outside: independent of the mind
senses.titleCN: 心外实物：不依赖心智而存在
senses.definition: real and existing independently of the mind, belonging to the object of knowledge rather than to the observer
senses.definitionCN: 真实存在、不依赖心智的，属于认知对象而非观察者的
senses.example: The mountain has an objective existence whether or not anyone looks at it.
senses.exampleCN: 无论是否有人看它，这座山都客观存在。
senses.why: From the mid-17th century the 'object' was pushed outside: what is objective is what belongs to the thing known, not to the knower. The sense almost reverses the older one.
senses.whyCN: 从 17 世纪中期起，“对象”被推到心智之外：objective 的东西属于被认识的事物，而不属于认识者。这个义项几乎翻转了旧义。

senses.title: Without a Personal Lens: impartial
senses.titleCN: 不戴个人镜片：不偏不倚
senses.definition: not influenced by personal feelings, interests, or bias when judging
senses.definitionCN: 判断时不受个人情感、利益或偏见影响
senses.example: A judge must remain objective even when the case is emotionally charged.
senses.exampleCN: 即使案件牵动情绪，法官也必须保持客观。
senses.why: If truth belongs to the object, the observer should stop adding private colour. The 18th-century sense, strengthened through German translations, names that disciplined detachment.
senses.whyCN: 如果真相属于对象，观察者就该停止添加私人色彩。18 世纪经德语译介强化的义项，命名的正是这种克制的抽离。

senses.title: What the Evidence Shows: fact-based
senses.titleCN: 证据所示：以事实为依据
senses.definition: based on observable facts and evidence that others can check
senses.definitionCN: 建立在他人可以核查的可观察事实与证据之上
senses.example: The report gives an objective account of the accident, with times and measurements.
senses.exampleCN: 报告用时间和测量数据，对事故作了客观陈述。
senses.why: An account is objective when it stays with what was put before the senses: times, measurements, records. Evidence replaces opinion as the measure.
senses.whyCN: 当陈述停留在摆在感官之前的东西——时间、测量、记录——它就是客观的。证据取代意见成为量尺。

senses.title: The Point to Be Taken: a military objective
senses.definition: a place or position that an army aims to capture or hold, from which the general noun use grew
senses.definitionCN: 军队意图夺取或守住的地点或阵地，名词的一般用法由此而来
senses.example: The hill was the objective of the night attack.
senses.exampleCN: 那座山头是夜袭的目标。
senses.why: Military language used objective for the point set before the force, the thing to be taken. The target on the map is literally 'the object put in front'.
senses.whyCN: 军事语言用 objective 指摆在部队前方的点，即要夺取的东西。地图上的目标字面上就是“被摆在前面的对象”。

senses.title: The Aim: a goal to reach
senses.definition: a goal or aim that a person or organization works toward
senses.definitionCN: 个人或组织努力要达到的目标
senses.example: Our main objective is to cut waiting times by half.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的主要目标是把等待时间减少一半。
senses.why: Once the military target became general, any planned end point could be an objective: something placed ahead of you that guides effort.
senses.whyCN: 军事目标一旦泛化，任何计划中的终点都可以叫 objective：一个摆在你前方、引导努力的东西。

senses.title: The Lens Facing the Object
senses.definition: in optics, the lens or lens system nearest the object being viewed, as in a microscope or telescope
senses.definitionCN: 光学中离被观察物体最近的那片透镜或透镜组，如显微镜或望远镜的物镜
senses.example: Clean the objective before examining the slide.
senses.exampleCN: 检查玻片前先清洁物镜。
senses.why: The optical objective is the lens turned toward the object, not toward the eye. The same 'thing before you' image is used in a physical instrument.
senses.whyCN: 光学物镜是朝向物体、而不是朝向眼睛的那片镜片。同一个“摆在面前的东西”的意象被用在一件实体仪器上。

senses.title: The Object Case: grammar
senses.definition: in grammar, the case of a noun or pronoun that is the object of a verb or preposition
senses.definitionCN: 语法中名词或代词作动词或介词宾语时的格
senses.example: In 'she saw him', him is in the objective case.
senses.exampleCN: 在 she saw him 中，him 是宾格。
senses.why: Grammar names the receiver of the action the object. The objective case is simply the form a word takes when it stands as the object before the verb.
senses.whyCN: 语法把动作的承受者称为 object。宾格就是当一个词作为动词的宾语出现时所取的形式。

senses.title: Description Without Interpretation
senses.titleCN: 不带解释的描述：客观呈现
senses.definition: presenting what can be seen or measured without adding interpretation, as in objective reporting or photography
senses.definitionCN: 只呈现可见或可测的内容而不添加解释，如客观报道或客观摄影
senses.example: The photographer took an objective record of the building before demolition.
senses.exampleCN: 摄影师在拆除前对建筑作了客观记录。
senses.why: The final extension keeps the observer out of the frame. What is recorded is the object as it stands, with no story laid over it.
senses.whyCN: 最后的延伸把观察者请出画面。被记录的是对象本来的样子，上面没有叠加任何故事。

intro.en: Objective is object plus -ive. Object came from Latin obiectum 'thing put before', and objective first meant 'existing as an object of thought' before its sense moved outside the mind to 'real' and then to 'impartial'.
intro.cn: objective 是 object 加 -ive。object 来自拉丁语 obiectum“被摆到面前的东西”，而 objective 最初指“作为思想对象而存在”，后来移出心智，变成“真实的”，再变成“不偏不倚的”。

items.en: First used as a philosophical term meaning 'as perceived or thought; ideal; representative; phenomenal', opposed to subjective or formal.
items.cn: 最初作哲学术语，意为“被感知或被思考的；观念的；表象的；现象的”，与 subjective 或 formal 相对。

items.en: The sense 'belonging to the real object of knowledge, real' appears, in contrast with subjective; the meaning almost reverses the earlier one.
items.cn: 出现“属于认知的实在对象、真实的”义，与 subjective 相对；含义几乎翻转了早先的义项。

items.en: The modern sense 'unbiased, not shaped by personal feeling' is strengthened through German philosophical translations.
items.cn: 现代义“客观的、不带偏见的”经德语哲学译介而强化。

items.en: Formed on medieval Latin objectivus, used by Duns Scotus, from objectum 'thing put before'.
items.cn: 按中世纪拉丁语 objectivus 构成，邓斯·司各脱曾使用，出自 objectum“被摆到面前的东西”。

items.en: Objectum is the neuter noun use of obiectus, past participle of obicere 'to throw before': ob 'in front of, towards, against' plus iacere 'to throw' (PIE *ye- 'to throw, impel').
items.cn: objectum 是 obiectus 的中性名词化；obiectus 为 obicere“投到前面”的过去分词：ob“在前、朝向、对着”+ iacere“投、掷”（原始印欧语 *ye-“投、推”）。

items.en: The noun 'objective' meaning a target comes from military usage, the point set before a force; the general sense 'goal' followed. Object itself dates from late 14c.
items.cn: 名词 objective 的“目标”义来自军事用语，即摆在部队前方的点；泛化的“目的”义随后出现。object 本身则始于 14 世纪晚期。

note.en: The look-alike group stays inside the object family and its -ive neighbours; the near-meaning group holds words that overlap with only part of objective.
note.cn: 形近组留在 object 词族及其 -ive 邻词内；近义组是只与 objective 部分义项重叠的词。

entries.definition: a thing that can be seen or touched, or something opposed. Objective is built from it, but the stress and the noun-verb split differ.
entries.definitionCN: 可见可触的物体，或反对的对象。objective 由它构成，但重音和名词／动词分工不同。

entries.definition: a statement of disagreement. It comes from object as a verb 'to oppose', not from objective.
entries.definitionCN: 反对的意见。它来自动词 object“反对”，而不是来自 objective。

entries.definition: a word that describes a noun. It shares the -ive ending and the Latin iacere 'throw' root, but its prefix is ad-, not ob-.
entries.definitionCN: 描述名词的词。它同样以 -ive 结尾，也含拉丁语 iacere“投”的词根，但前缀是 ad-，不是 ob-。

entries.definition: not favouring one side over another. It stresses fairness between parties, while objective stresses independence from one's own feelings.
entries.definitionCN: 不偏袒任何一方。它强调各方之间的公平，objective 强调独立于自己的情感。

entries.definition: free from prejudice or a settled leaning. It is close to objective but names the absence of bias rather than the presence of facts.
entries.definitionCN: 没有偏见或既定倾向。它接近 objective，但说的是“没有偏见”，而不是“依据事实”。

entries.definition: based on facts. It covers only the evidence sense of objective and says nothing about being a goal.
entries.definitionCN: 以事实为依据的。它只覆盖 objective 的证据义，与“目标”义无关。

normalIntro.en: Real links only: objectum is ob- 'before' plus iacere 'to throw', and objective is object plus -ive. The 1610s and modern senses are a recorded reversal, not an invented story.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实联系：objectum 是 ob-“在前”加 iacere“投”，objective 是 object 加 -ive。17 世纪初义与现代义是有记录的翻转，不是编造的故事。

normal.en: Objectum is ob- 'in front of' plus iacere 'to throw': a thing thrown before the mind or the eyes.
normal.cn: objectum 是 ob-“在前”加 iacere“投”：被投到心智或视线之前的东西。

normal.en: Objective is simply object plus -ive: 'relating to the object put before you'.
normal.cn: objective 就是 object 加 -ive：与“摆在你面前的对象”相关的。

normal.en: The 1610s sense meant 'in the mind'; the modern sense moved outside the mind to 'real'. The word reversed direction.
normal.cn: 17 世纪初的义项指“在心中的”；现代义移到心外，指“真实的”。这个词转了个方向。

normal.en: Objection and objective share object but pull opposite ways: one throws something against, the other looks at what is before.
normal.cn: objection 与 objective 都含 object，却朝相反方向拉：一个把东西扔过去反对，一个只看面前的东西。

normal.en: A military objective is the literal point set before a force; the everyday 'goal' grew from that target.
normal.cn: 军事 objective 是字面上摆在部队前方的点；日常的“目标”义从那个靶点长出来。

abstract.en: Picture an object alone under a lamp: the table, the wall and the observer all fall into shadow.
abstract.cn: 想象灯下只有一件东西：桌子、墙和观察者都落进阴影。

abstract.en: The observer steps back until their own shadow leaves the frame; that is the move from subjective to objective.
abstract.cn: 观察者后退，直到自己的影子离开画面；这就是从主观到客观的那一步。

abstract.en: Move the same object onto a map and it becomes a target: objective is now the point to be reached.
abstract.cn: 把同一件东西移到地图上，它就成了靶点：objective 此时是要到达的点。

examples.en: The study offers an objective measure of how noisy the streets are.
examples.cn: 这项研究提供了街道噪声程度的客观量度。

examples.en: Our objective for the year is to reduce waste by a third.
examples.cn: 我们今年的目标是把浪费减少三分之一。

examples.en: He tried to stay objective, but the photographs made him angry.
examples.cn: 他努力保持客观，但那些照片让他愤怒。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啊不，接个物体」——先别急着评判，把摆在面前的物体接住看清楚 → objective 客观的、目标

root: 拉丁语 objectum“被摆到面前的东西”= ob“在前”+ iacere“投、掷”，加 -ive；objective 字面“与摆在面前的对象相关的”，由“客体”引出“客观”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of objective all turn on one act: throwing something in front. First it is an object of thought, then a real thing outside, then an impartial view, then a target on a map.
sensesIntro.cn: objective 的九个义项都围绕一个动作：把某物投到前方。它先是思想的对象，再是心外的实物，再是不偏不倚的看法，最后成为地图上的靶点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an object placed in front of the mind or the eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件被摆到心智或视线之前的东西。

branches.en: THE OBJECT IN THE MIND: the 1610s philosophical sense, where the object is still a thought.
branches.cn: 心中的对象：17 世纪初的哲学义，对象仍是一种思想。

branches.en: REALITY AND EVIDENCE: the object outside the mind, and the facts that can be checked.
branches.cn: 现实与证据：心外的对象，以及可以核查的事实。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINED OBSERVER: impartial judgment, and description without interpretation.
branches.cn: 受约束的观察者：不偏不倚的判断，以及不带解释的描述。

branches.en: THE AIM: a military point to be taken, and the general goal that grew from it.
branches.cn: 目标：要夺取的军事据点，以及由此长出的普通目的。

branches.en: TECHNICAL OBJECTS: the lens facing the object, and the grammatical object case.
branches.cn: 技术性对象：朝向物体的镜片，以及语法中的宾格。

intro.en: Objective is the Latin adjective objectivus in English form: object- plus -ive. The root sits in ob- 'before' and iacere 'to throw', the same root that gives subject, adjective and object.
intro.cn: objective 是拉丁形容词 objectivus 的英语形式：object- 加 -ive。词根在 ob-“在前”与 iacere“投”里，也是 subject、adjective、object 的共同来源。

latinIntro.en: Latin objectum 'thing put before' is the neuter noun from obicere; objectivus was used by Duns Scotus. The same iacere also builds subjectum 'thrown under' and adiectivus 'thrown to'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 objectum“被摆到前面之物”是 obicere 的中性名词；objectivus 由邓斯·司各脱使用。同一个 iacere 还构成 subjectum“投在下面”和 adiectivus“投向”。

items.meaning: relating to the object; impartial; a goal
items.meaningCN: 与对象相关的；客观的；目标（-ive 构成形容词，也可作名词）
items.example: The review aims to be objective.

items.meaningCN: 客观地；不带偏见地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The team judged the design objectively.
items.exampleCN: 团队客观地评估了这项设计。

items.meaningCN: 客观性；无偏见（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: Journalists are expected to maintain objectivity.

items.meaning: a thing put before the senses; to oppose
items.meaningCN: 物体；对象；反对（ob-“在前”+ iect“投”）
items.example: A strange object lay on the path.
items.exampleCN: 小路上躺着一个奇怪的物体。

items.meaning: a statement thrown against something; disagreement
items.meaningCN: 异议；反对（-ion 构成动作名词）

items.meaning: to treat as an object or make concrete
items.meaningCN: 使物化；使具体化（-ify 构成动词）
items.example: The advertisement objectifies the people it shows.
items.exampleCN: 这则广告把画面中的人物化了。

items.meaning: the act of treating someone as an object
items.meaningCN: 物化；对象化（-ication 构成名词）
items.example: The essay discusses the objectification of labour.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章讨论劳动的物化。

items.meaning: literally 'thrown to'; a word added to a noun
items.meaningCN: 字面“投向”；形容词（加在名词上的词）
items.example: Choose a precise adjective for the noun.
items.exampleCN: 为这个名词选一个准确的形容词。

items.meaning: literally 'thrown under'; a topic or a grammatical subject
items.meaningCN: 字面“投在下面”；主题；主语
items.example: The subject of the talk was water.

items.meaning: based on personal feeling rather than the object

latinEntries.meaning: relating to an object; existing as an object of thought
latinEntries.meaningCN: 与对象相关的；作为思想对象存在的（邓斯·司各脱用语）

definition_zh: 义务（良心或道德上必须履行的事）；法律义务（法令、合同或规章所规定的作为或不作为）；债务（必须偿付的款项或必须提供的给付）；人情债（受恩之后觉得应当回报的亏欠感）；约束力（誓约、承诺或规则对人的拘束力量）；受托职责（因担任职务而必须尽到的义务）；契据债券（以文书形式承认的付款义务）；被迫感（觉得别无选择、只能去做的心理压力）
definition_en: a binding requirement, whether moral, legal or contractual, that a person is bound to carry out or to pay
core_image: 一根绳子一头系在人的手腕上，另一头系在一张写满条款的纸上，风吹得纸响，绳子始终不松
scene: 公证处的窗口前，一位老人把一份发黄的借据摊在桌上，说当年借钱的人已经去世，他的儿子仍然每年送来利息。The obligation had outlived the man who signed it.
sceneCN: 这里 obligation 指「按字据必须偿付的债务」（第 3 个义项：必须偿付的款项）；句意为这笔债比签字的人活得更久。可辨识物件：发黄的借据、窗口玻璃、红色印章、利息收条；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 义务；法律责任；债务；人情债；约束力；受托职责

forms.label: 形容词（受约束的；承蒙的）

senses.title: A duty felt in conscience
senses.definition: a duty that a person feels bound in conscience to perform, even when no one can compel it
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在良心上觉得必须履行、即使无人能强制也必须做的义务
senses.example: She felt an obligation to tell the family what she had seen.
senses.exampleCN: 她觉得有义务把自己看到的事告诉这家人。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to bind, so the word pictures a person tied to a task before any law appears.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词意为「捆绑」，所以这个词描绘的是在法律出现之前，一个人就已经被系在一件事上。

senses.title: A duty imposed by law or contract
senses.titleCN: 法律或合同规定的义务
senses.definition: a requirement that a statute, contract or official rule lays on a person and that can be enforced
senses.definitionCN: 由法令、合同或正式规章加于某人、并且可以被强制执行的作为或不作为要求
senses.example: The lease imposes an obligation to repair the roof by June.
senses.exampleCN: 租约规定了一项在六月前修好屋顶的义务。
senses.why: Once a court can enforce the bond, the image of a rope becomes a legal relation with a remedy.
senses.whyCN: 一旦法院可以强制执行这根绳子，捆绑的图景就变成带有救济手段的法律关系。

senses.title: A debt that must be paid
senses.definition: a sum of money or a service that one is bound to pay or provide to another
senses.definitionCN: 必须向他人偿付的款项，或必须向他人提供的给付
senses.example: The obligation had outlived the man who signed it.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔债比签字的人活得更久。
senses.why: Bonds are most often counted in money, so the general binding became a figure on a ledger.
senses.whyCN: 捆绑最常见于金钱，于是这种一般的约束就变成账本上的一个数字。

senses.title: A debt of gratitude
senses.definition: the sense of owing something back after receiving help or kindness that cannot be repaid in full
senses.definitionCN: 得到帮助或恩惠之后，觉得应当回报、却又无法完全还清的那种亏欠感
senses.example: He stayed to look after the old teacher out of a sense of obligation.
senses.exampleCN: 他留下来照顾那位老教师，是出于一份人情上的亏欠感。
senses.why: Kindness can bind as firmly as a contract, and English uses the same word for both ties.
senses.whyCN: 恩惠能像合同一样把人系住，英语对这两种束缚用了同一个词。

senses.title: The binding force of a promise
senses.titleCN: 誓约与规则具有的约束力
senses.definition: the force that a promise, oath or rule has in holding a person to a stated course of action
senses.definitionCN: 誓约、承诺或规则把一个人固定在既定做法上的那股力量
senses.example: The oath carried an obligation that he could not easily set aside.
senses.exampleCN: 那个誓约带着一种约束力，他无法轻易搁下。
senses.why: Here the noun names not the task but the pull that keeps a person from walking away.
senses.whyCN: 这里名词指的不是任务，而是不让一个人走开的那股拉力。

senses.title: Duties attached to a trust or office
senses.titleCN: 受托或任职所带来的职责
senses.definition: the specific duties that a person must perform because of a post or a trust accepted
senses.definitionCN: 因担任某个职位或接受某项托付而必须履行的具体职责
senses.example: A trustee's obligations include keeping accounts open to inspection.
senses.exampleCN: 受托人的职责包括保存可供查阅的账目。
senses.why: A post adds its own set, so the general bond becomes a list that other people can check.
senses.whyCN: 一个职位自带一整套要求，于是笼统的捆绑变成别人可以核对的清单。

senses.title: A sealed bond or written undertaking
senses.titleCN: 契据形式的债券与承诺书
senses.definition: in law, a written document under seal by which a person binds himself to pay a sum or to perform an act
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上指加盖印章的文书，当事人在其中承诺付款或履行某项行为
senses.example: The estate settled the obligation recorded in the bond.
senses.exampleCN: 遗产管理人清偿了债券上记载的那笔债务。
senses.why: The word once named the paper itself, because the paper was the thing that did the binding.
senses.whyCN: 这个词曾经直接指那张纸，因为起捆绑作用的就是那张纸。

senses.title: The felt pressure of having no choice
senses.definition: the state of feeling compelled to act, whether or not one agrees with the act
senses.definitionCN: 觉得不得不做某事的状态，不论自己是否认同这件事
senses.example: He signed the form under obligation, not out of any belief in the scheme.
senses.exampleCN: 他在被迫的情况下签了表格，并不是因为相信这个方案。
senses.why: When the tie is felt from the inside, the noun describes a pressure rather than a duty owed.
senses.whyCN: 当这根绳子从内部被感受到时，这个名词描述的是压力，而不是欠下的义务。

intro.en: Obligation comes from Latin obligare 'to bind, tie up', built on ob- 'towards, against' and ligare 'to bind'. The noun obligatio passed through Old French into English, keeping both the moral and the legal sense.
intro.cn: obligation 来自拉丁 obligare「捆绑、约束」，由 ob-「朝向、对着」与 ligare「绑」构成。名词 obligatio 经古法语进入英语，同时保留了道德与法律两层意思。

items.en: Ligare meant 'to bind, tie'. It also gives ligament and ligature, where the same root names things that fasten; its deeper origin is not established, so any earlier form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: ligare 意为「绑、系」。它同样给出 ligament 与 ligature，同一个词根在两词中指起固定作用的东西；其更深的来源未获证明，凡为其提出的更早形式都属重构形式。

items.en: Ob- 'towards, against' plus ligare formed obligare, 'to bind towards someone', hence to put a person under a duty. The prefix marks the direction of the tie, not its strength.
items.cn: ob-「朝向、对着」加 ligare 构成 obligare，意为「朝某人绑过去」，引申为使某人负上义务。前缀标的是捆绑的方向，而不是力度。

items.en: The noun obligatio named both the act of binding and the bond itself; Roman law used it for a tie that could be enforced by an action.
items.cn: 名词 obligatio 既指捆绑的动作，也指束缚本身；罗马法用它指可以通过诉讼强制执行的约束关系。

items.en: Old French obligation carried the moral sense of a duty and the legal sense of a bond, and English adopted it in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 obligation 兼有道德义务与法律债券两层意思，英语在十四世纪借入。

items.en: English law kept the written-bond sense, and the everyday moral sense grew beside it; obligation to and under an obligation are the modern frames that separate them.
items.cn: 英国法保留了文书债券的义项，日常的道德义在旁边生长；后接表示对象的介词，与「负有义务」这一固定说法，正是今天区分两者的框架。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin of ligare and the English date): the link with religion is real but semantic only, since religio is generally explained as re- plus ligare in the sense of binding fast, while ally and alliance come from ad- plus ligare with a different prefix and a different sense, and obligation shares the root with religion without sharing any meaning.
items.cn: 来源不确定（ligare 的更深来源与英语首见年代）：与 religion 的联系确实存在，但只在词根层面，因为 religio 一般被解释为 re- 加 ligare、取「紧紧绑住」之意，而 ally 与 alliance 则出自 ad- 加 ligare，前缀不同、语义也不同；obligation 与 religion 共享词根，却没有任何义项上的关系。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same binding root, each with a different prefix or ending, so the meanings diverge sharply; group two holds nouns that also put a person under a demand, with a different source for that demand.
note.cn: 第一组同出「绑」这个词根，但前缀或词尾各不相同，语义因此分得很开；第二组是同样把人置于某种要求之下的名词，只是要求的来源不同。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun: to bind someone by law, by duty or by a favour done, and in polite use simply to do someone a kindness.
entries.definitionCN: 这个名词背后的动词：以法律、义务或恩惠把人绑住；在客套用法中则只表示帮某人一个忙。

entries.definition: Made from the noun with the ending -ory, meaning required rather than optional; it describes the requirement, not the person under it.
entries.definitionCN: 由这个名词加表示「具有……性质的」词尾构成，意为强制的而非可选的；它描述要求本身，而不是被要求的人。

entries.definition: Built on ligare with a different stem: it names the band that binds a joint, and the binding here is physical.
entries.definitionCN: 以 ligare 加另一个词干构成：它指把关节绑住的韧带，这里的捆绑是身体上的。

entries.definition: Generally explained as re- plus ligare, 'to bind fast'; it shares the root but has no sense relation to a duty or a debt.
entries.definitionCN: 一般解释为 re- 加 ligare「紧紧绑住」；它与本词共享词根，却与义务、债务没有任何义项关系。

entries.definition: From ad- 'to' plus ligare, 'to bind to one side'; it names a partner joined by agreement, and the prefix, not the root, does the work.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 ad-「向」加 ligare「绑到一边」；它指因约定而结合的伙伴，起作用的是前缀而不是词根。

entries.definition: What a person owes by law, by office or by conscience; duty is the content, while obligation stresses the tie that holds the person to it.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人依法、依职或依良知所欠之事；义务是内容，而 obligation 强调把人系在这件事上的那根绳子。

entries.definition: A promise or engagement a person has taken on, usually by choice; obligation can be imposed without consent.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人通常自愿承担下来的承诺或投入；obligation 则可以在未经同意时被加于身上。

entries.definition: Legal responsibility for a debt or damage, measured in money; it is the narrow financial end of obligation.
entries.definitionCN: 对债务或损害承担的法律责任，以金钱衡量；它是 obligation 最窄的财务一端。

entries.definition: A condition that must be met, often written into a rule or a contract; it names the condition, not the bond that makes it binding.
entries.definitionCN: 必须满足的条件，常写入规则或合同；它指条件本身，而不是使其具有约束力的那根绳子。

entries.definition: The state of having to answer for something; it looks at who must explain, while obligation looks at what binds them to act.
entries.definitionCN: 必须为某事作出交代的状态；它着眼的是该由谁解释，而 obligation 着眼的是把人绑向行动的东西。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin verb of binding, its prefix, the real family, the real phrases, and the relatives that share the root but carry different prefixes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「捆绑」动词、它的前缀、真实的词族、真实的搭配，以及共享词根却带不同前缀的亲戚。

normal.en: Ob- means towards and ligare means to bind, so an obligation is a rope tied towards a task.
normal.cn: ob- 意为「朝向」，ligare 意为「绑」，所以义务就是一根朝某件事绑过去的绳子。

normal.en: The family runs oblige, obliged, obliging, obligatory, obligatorily and obligee.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 oblige、obliged、obliging、obligatory、obligatorily 与 obligee。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the frames: a legal obligation, under an obligation to, fulfil an obligation, without obligation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显出常用框架：法律义务、有义务去做、履行义务、不附带义务。

normal.en: The same root appears with other prefixes: a ligament binds a joint, religion binds fast, and an ally is bound to one side.
normal.cn: 同一个词根配上别的前缀：ligament 绑住关节，religion 取「紧紧绑住」之意，ally 则是被绑到一边的伙伴。

normal.en: Obligation is what ties a person to act; responsibility is what a person must answer for afterwards.
normal.cn: obligation 是把人绑向行动的东西，responsibility 则是事后必须为之作答的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a rope running from a wrist to a sheet of clauses, slack enough to move but never loose enough to slip off.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子从手腕连到一页条款上，松到可以活动，却绝不会松脱。

abstract.en: Picture a signed card in a coat pocket that grows heavier with every year it is carried.
abstract.cn: 想象外套口袋里一张签过字的卡片，带得越久就越沉。

abstract.en: Picture two posts with a rope stretched between them, so that walking past means ducking under it.
abstract.cn: 想象两根柱子之间拉着一根绳，走过那里就得低头钻过去。

examples.en: Members are under an obligation to declare any outside income.
examples.cn: 成员有义务申报任何外部收入。

examples.en: He helped her move, and she now feels an obligation to return the favour.
examples.cn: 他帮她搬了家，她现在觉得欠着一份应当回报的人情。

examples.en: The bond is an obligation enforceable in court.
examples.cn: 这张债券是一项可以在法院强制执行的义务。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「朝向 + 绑」——把你朝某件事绑过去的那根绳子，就是义务；绳子换成钱，就是债务

root: 拉丁 obligare「捆绑、约束」= ob-（朝向、对着）+ ligare「绑」；名词 obligatio 经古法语 obligation 进入英语。同根词有 ligament、ligature、religion（re- 加 ligare，紧紧绑住）、ally 与 alliance（ad- 加 ligare）；前缀不同，语义各异。ligare 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one rope: conscience ties it, law tightens it, money counts it, gratitude feels it, the noun then names the force itself, lists the duties of a post, records it as a sealed bond, and finally describes the pressure of being pulled from inside.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一根绳子展开：良心先把它系上，法律把它收紧，金钱把它算成数目，感恩从内部感到它；随后名词指这股力量本身、列出职位的职责、把它记成盖章的债券，最后描述被从内部拉扯的压力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope from a wrist to a page of clauses, slack enough to move but never loose enough to slip off.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根从手腕连到条款纸页的绳子，松到可以活动，却绝不会松脱。

branches.en: INNER TIE AND ITS FORCE: the duty felt and the binding power that holds a person are one rope seen as content and as strength.
branches.cn: 内在的系与它的力：被感受到的义务与把人固定的力量，是同一根绳子作为内容与作为力度的一面。

branches.en: PAPER AND LAW: a statute and a sealed bond are two ways of writing the tie down.
branches.cn: 纸与法：法令与盖章债券，是把这根绳子写下来的两种方式。

branches.en: TWO KINDS OF DEBT: money can be counted and repaid, while gratitude cannot.
branches.cn: 两种债：钱可以算清也可以还清，恩情却不行。

branches.en: THE POST: an office supplies its own list of duties, which other people can inspect.
branches.cn: 职位：一个岗位自带一份职责清单，别人可以逐项核对。

branches.en: PULLED FROM INSIDE: when the rope is felt rather than owed, the word names compulsion.
branches.cn: 从内部被拉：当绳子是被感受到而不是被欠下时，这个词指的就是被迫。

intro.en: Obligation reads as a prefix of direction, a root meaning to bind, and a noun ending that names the resulting state or instrument.
intro.cn: obligation 可以读成表示方向的前缀、意为「绑」的词根，以及指称由此形成的状态或文书的名称词尾。

latinIntro.en: The root ligare also gives ligament, ligature, religion, ally and alliance; ob- marks direction towards, while re- and ad- give those other words their different senses.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 ligare 还给出 ligament、ligature、religion、ally 与 alliance；ob- 标出「朝向」，re- 与 ad- 则让其余各词各有不同语义。

items.example: The prefix shows the direction in which the binding is done.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀指出捆绑是朝哪个方向做的。

items.example: The root supplies the physical picture of a rope.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供绳子的具体形象。

items.meaning: to bind towards; to put under a duty
items.example: The verb turns a literal rope into a duty owed to a person.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把字面的绳子变成对某人的义务。

items.example: The Latin noun names both the act and the tie it creates.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词既指动作，也指动作造成的束缚。

items.meaning: a duty; a debt; a bond
items.example: The obligation had outlived the man who signed it.
items.exampleCN: 这笔债比签字的人活得更久。

items.example: Attendance at the safety briefing is obligatory.
items.exampleCN: 参加安全说明会是强制性的。

items.meaning: to bind by duty; to do a kindness
items.example: The rules oblige the carrier to inspect every crate.
items.exampleCN: 规则要求承运方检查每一个板条箱。

items.meaning: the person to whom a bond is owed
items.example: The obligee may demand payment on the stated date.
items.exampleCN: 债权人可以在约定日期要求付款。
